L1525: ## Conclusion
L1526: - Bexagliflozin exposures increased with increasing severity of renal impairment, with a 54% increase in bexagliflozin AUC for subjects with severe renal impairment.
- In patients with moderate and severe renal impairment, UGE values reduced by 60% and 80% compared to patients with normal renal function.
L1527: ***FDA Reviewer Comment:*** Per the Applicant “Because only a very small fraction of bexagliflozin is found in urine, the increase in systemic exposure with decreasing renal function substantially implicates the kidney as an important organ for metabolism of bexagliflozin. However, exposure to both the principal glucuronide and the most prominent oxidative metabolite increased with decreasing renal function, suggesting that the reduction in elimination falls more rapidly than the reduction in capacity to metabolize bexagliflozin.”
L1528: ## 14.2.9. Effect of Probenecid, Rifampin, and Verapamil on PK/PD of Bexagliflozin (Trial C-454)
L1529: ## Study Design
L1530: This was a phase 1, open-label, nonrandomized, fixed sequence composite study to assess the effects of probenecid, rifampin, and verapamil on the PK and PD of orally administered bexagliflozin tablets in 48 healthy subjects (N=16 per cohort).
L1531: ## Cohort 1: Bexagliflozin/Probenecid (UGT Inhibitor):
L1532: - On Day 1, subjects took one 20 mg bexagliflozin tablet; on Days 3 to 4 subjects took probenecid tablets, 500 mg (twice daily [BID]); on Day 5 subjects took one bexagliflozin tablet (once daily [QD]) + probenecid tablets, 500 mg (BID); and on Day 6 subjects took probenecid tablets, 500 mg (BID).
L1533: ## Cohort 2: Bexagliflozin/Rifampin (CYP3A/UGT Inducer)
L1534: - On Day 1, subjects took one bexagliflozin tablet, 20 mg; on Days 3 to 5 subjects took 600 mg of rifampin (2 x 300 mg capsules) QD; on Day 6 subjects took one bexagliflozin tablet, 20 mg, and 600 mg of rifampin; and on Day 7 subjects took 600 mg of rifampin.
L1535: ## Cohort 3: Bexagliflozin/Verapamil (P-gp Inhibitor)
L1536: - On Day 1, subjects took one bexagliflozin tablet, 20 mg; and on Day 4 subjects took one verapamil tablet, 120 mg, 1 hour before taking one bexagliflozin tablet, 20 mg.
L1537: Multiple PK and urine samples were collected for 48 hours after administration of bexagliflozin on Day 1 (bexagliflozin alone) and Day 4/5/6 (bexagliflozin + perpetrator drug).
L1538: ## Results
L1539: - *Cohort 1:* Previous studies have indicated that bexagliflozin is cleared predominantly by metabolism to an inactive metabolite, bexagliflozin 3'-O-glucuronide (EGT0002149), by UGT1A9. When bexagliflozin was coadministered with probenecid, a nonspecific UGT inhibitor, 39% and 44% increases in AUC of bexagliflozin and EGT0002149, respectively, were observed (Table 111). Postdose UGE for each 12-hour collection interval was similar for both treatments, indicating that the inhibitory effect on bexagliflozin exposure by probenecid had no effect on UGE.
- *Cohort 2:* Rifampin is a strong inducer of CYP3A4 and several UGT enzymes, including UGT1A9. When bexagliflozin was coadministered with rifampin, its AUC0-t decreased by 14% and Cmax increased by 20% (Table 111). This was accompanied by a decreased bexagliflozin t1/2 from 12.9 hours to 5.9 hours. Coadministration with rifampin led to 90% (90% CI: 145%, 250%) and 54% (90% CI: 119%, 199%) increases in EGT0002149 Cmax and AUC, respectively. UGE0-24h was comparable between treatments.
- *Cohort 3:* Verapamil is a P-glycoprotein (P-gp) inhibitor. The point estimate and the 90% CI for both Cmax and AUC were entirely contained within the range of 80 to 125%, indicating that there was no interaction between bexagliflozin and verapamil (Table 111).

L1543: ## Conclusions
L1544: Bexagliflozin is not expected to interact to a clinically relevant extent with other drugs that are inhibitors of P-gp and UGTs.
L1545: **Reviewer's Comment:** Coadministration with UGT inhibitor probenecid is expected to decrease the concentrations of EGT0002149, a UGT metabolite of bexagliflozin. The unexpected 40% increase of this metabolite is likely because it is also subject to active transport by uptake transporters such as OAT3, which are inhibited by probenecid.
L1546: In this study, rifampin was only dosed for 3 days before coadministration with bexagliflozin. The current study may not adequately capture the worst-case scenario of enzyme induction.
L1547: ## 14.2.10. Effect of Exenatide on Bexagliflozin (Trial C-458)
L1548: ## Study Design
L1549: This was a phase 1, open-label, two-period, two-treatment crossover study to assess the effects of exenatide injection on the PK and PD of orally administered bexagliflozin tablets. Twenty eligible healthy subjects were randomly assigned to one of two groups (N=10 per group). Each group received both the treatments, alternately, in a crossover fashion, with the two treatment periods separated by a 7-day washout period.
L1550: - A single oral dose of 20 mg bexagliflozin administered 30 minutes after breakfast
- Exenatide at 10 µg BID with an initial dose 30 minutes prior bexagliflozin administration, and 1 hour before breakfast, followed by the second dose of exenatide alone 1 hour prior to the evening meal
L1551: Blood and urine samples were collected at multiple timepoints for up to 48 hours postdose.
L1552: ## Results
L1553: - Absorption was delayed when bexagliflozin was administered 30 minutes after exenatide injection as evident in the time-concentration profile and a prolonged T_{max} of 5.00 hours postdose compared to 2.00 hours postdose for administration of bexagliflozin alone (Figure 30). Additionally, AUC_{0-t} and C_{max} of bexagliflozin were increased by approximately 48% and 25%, respectively, compared to bexagliflozin administration alone (Table 112).
- UGE during the first 12 hours after dosing was lower in subjects administered bexagliflozin + exenatide (26 g) compared to when subjects were administered bexagliflozin alone (38 g), with comparable UGE observed between treatments for the subsequent postdose collection intervals (Table 113).
- Approximately 65% of the total UGE was excreted in the first 24 hours for each treatment dosing period.

Source: Table 13 in Study Report THR-1442-C-458
L1563: ## Conclusion
L1564: No clinically significant DDI was observed when bexagliflozin was administered with exenatide.
L1565: ***FDA Reviewer Comment:*** *Rationale of DDI study: Exenatide is one of most prescribed GLP-1 receptor agonists and is administered subcutaneously (SC) BID because of its relatively short half-life of 2.4 hours. Exenatide is primarily eliminated by glomerular filtration and subsequent proteolytic degradation, thus, interactions involving CYP450 isoenzymes or enzymes responsible for phase 2 metabolism are not expected. However, because exenatide slows gastric emptying, the rate of absorption for concurrent orally administered medications may be altered.*
L1566: *Exenatide increased bexagliflozin AUC and Cmax by 30 to 40%. Given metabolism based DDI is not likely, the increased exposures of bexagliflozin are likely due to prolonged GI emptying, a mechanism similar to the observed higher bioavailability from the delayed release formulation than the immediate release formulation. Nonetheless, the 30 to 40% increase in bexagliflozin is not considered clinically relevant in terms of safety.*
L1567: *Exenatide induces glucose-dependent insulin secretion and suppresses postprandial glucagon release and therefore may accelerate the absorption of glucose in peripheral tissue via insulin action. This mechanism likely reduces the filtered glucose in the kidney and results in reduced glucose. The observed ~30% reduction in first 0- to 12-hour UGE when bexagliflozin was administered with exenatide may not be clinically relevant.*
L1568: ## 14.2.11. Effect of Bexagliflozin on the PK of Metformin, Glimepiride or Sitagliptin (Trial C-453)
L1569: ## Study Design
L1570: This was a phase 1, open-label, three-period, three-treatment crossover study designed to assess the effects of bexagliflozin on the PK of metformin, glimepiride, and sitagliptin. Fifty-four eligible healthy subjects were randomly assigned to one of three groups (N=18 per group).
L1571: - Group 1: bexagliflozin /metformin
- Group 2: bexagliflozin /glimepiride
- Group 3: bexagliflozin /sitagliptin
L1572: For each group, every subject received a single dose of bexagliflozin tablet, 20 mg, alone, a single dose of an oral hypoglycemic agent (OHA: 1000 mg metformin, 2 mg glimepiride, or 100 mg sitagliptin) alone, and the combination of both (bexagliflozin tablet and OHA) alternately in a crossover fashion, with three treatment periods separated by a washout period of at least 7 days. PK and urine samples were collected for up to 48- and 72-hours postdose for groups 1 and 2, and group 3, respectively.
L1573: ## Results
L1574: - The Impact of Metformin, Glimepiride, and Sitagliptin on Bexagliflozin PK
L1575: The estimated geometric mean ratios and 90% CI of bexagliflozin AUC were within the 80% to 125%, when taken with metformin, glimepiride, or sitagliptin (Table 114). The point estimate and 90% CI of bexagliflozin C_{max} slightly fell outside of the bounds of 80-125%, when taken with sitagliptin and glimepiride. Nonetheless, the extent of exposure change is not considered as clinically significant.
L1576: - The Impact of Bexagliflozin on the PK of Metformin, Glimepiride, and Sitagliptin
L1577: There was no impact on the PK of metformin or sitagliptin when taken with bexagliflozin, as the point estimate and corresponding 90% CI for C_{max} and AUC were entirely contained within the 80-125% margins (Table 115). Glimepiride AUC_{0-4} increased by 27% (90% CI: 10%, 48%) in the presence of bexagliflozin. The extent of exposure increase in glimepiride is not clinically relevant.
L1578: - UGE values of bexagliflozin were slightly lower when administered with other antidiabetic agents but were not statistically significantly different.

L1589: ## 14.2.12. Dose-Finding Study Using FPG (Trial C-402)
L1590: ## Study Design
L1591: This was a phase 2 study to evaluate the efficacy of bexagliflozin based on FPG in patients with T2DM. The study included two segments:
L1592: - Segment 1: a single-center, open label, ascending dose study in four groups of diabetic subjects (5 per group) who received 5, 10, 20, or 50 mg of bexagliflozin capsules orally once daily for 28 days. The subjects were housed overnight in clinic for the first 3 days for safety and PK evaluation.
- Segment 2: a multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled parallel group study in five groups of diabetic subjects (25 per group) who receive oral bexagliflozin capsules at 5, 10, 20, or 50 mg/day or placebo once daily for 28 days in an outpatient setting.
L1593: ## Results
L1594: - PK: Cmax and AUC were dose proportional over the dose range of 5 to 50 mg (data not shown).
- Reductions in FPG ranged from -24.25 to -41.64 mg/dL in the bexagliflozin treatment groups and was -6.63 mg/dL in the placebo group. Significant differences versus placebo were observed for both the 20 mg and 50 mg bexagliflozin groups.
- Increases in total UGE for all bexagliflozin treatment groups versus placebo were observed after one and 28 days of treatment. The change from baseline to Day 28 ranged from 18.71 to 26.80 g/24 h in the bexagliflozin cohorts versus -0.2 g/24 h with placebo (data not shown). The UGE values for all bexagliflozin cohorts were highly significant (p&lt;0.0001).

L1614: ## Conclusion
L1615: The changes in FPG were determined in T2DM patients at bexagliflozin doses ranging from 5 mg to 50 mg in a 28-day study (Figure 32). Based on the fitted E_{max} model, the 20-mg dose is expected to produce ~90% of the maximum effect in lowering FPG.
L1616: *FDA Reviewer Comment: No apparent dose-response on UGE was observed in this study likely because of highly variable UGE among T2DM patients.*
L1617: ## 14.2.13. Dose-Finding Study by HbA1c (Trial C-449)
L1618: ## Study Design
L1619: The was a phase 2b multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled parallel group study to assess the effect of once daily bexagliflozin at doses ranging from 5-mg to 20-mg tablets for 12 weeks on HbA1c in either treatment-naïve T2DM subjects or in subjects who were treated with one oral antidiabetic agent. The primary efficacy endpoint was change from baseline in HbA1c after 12 weeks of placebo or bexagliflozin treatment. The secondary efficacy endpoint included FPG, seated systolic blood pressure (SBP) and diastolic blood pressure (DBP) and body weight.
L1620: Figure 33. Trial Design, Trial C-449
L1621: Source: Figure 1 of Study Report THR-1442-C-449
Abbreviations: FU, follow-up; OHA oral hypoglycemic agent; Txt, therapy.
L1622: ## Results
L1623: - A dose-dependent reduction in HbA1c over 12 weeks was observed with bexagliflozin doses ranging from 5 mg to 20 mg (Figure 34). All decreases in percent HbA1c were statistically significant and clinically meaningful.
- The proportions of subjects who achieved a postbaseline HbA1c &lt;7% were 15% in placebo and 21%, 22%, and 36% in bexagliflozin 5 mg, 10 mg, and 20 mg treatment groups, respectively.
- A dose-dependent decrease in FPG from baseline to Week 12 was observed with the maximum mean decrease of -1.240 (SD 1.2305) mmol/L in the bexagliflozin 20 mg group.
- Daily dosing of bexagliflozin tablets for 12 weeks was well tolerated. Among all groups, subjects with related TEAEs were higher in the 20 mg bexagliflozin group (22.4%) compared to the related events in the 5 mg bexagliflozin (8.3%), 10 mg bexagliflozin (6.9%), or placebo (8.3%) groups (Table 117)

L1638: ## 14.2.14. Effects on QT Prolongation (Trial C-428)
L1639: ## Study Design
L1640: This was a phase 1, single-center, randomized, partially double-blind, three-treatment, three-period study designed to assess the effects of a single dose of bexagliflozin capsule on QTc interval in 36 healthy male and female subjects. Subjects were assigned to receive single oral doses of placebo, 100 mg bexagliflozin, and 400 mg moxifloxacin in a randomized order (single dose of drug/placebo given during each treatment period), with a minimum 7-day washout interval between each drug administration. All three treatments were administered in the fasted state. Blood samples were collected for up to 24 hours.

L1652: ## 14.3. Pharmacometrics Review
L1653: ## 14.3.1. Review Summary
L1654: In general, the Applicant's population pharmacokinetic (popPK) analysis is considered acceptable for describing bexagliflozin PK (sustained-release or SR formulation for commercialization) in healthy subjects and those with T2DM. The final popPK model is adequate for assessing the impact of clinically relevant covariates on drug exposure and supporting labeling statements. The Applicant's popPK analyses were verified by the reviewer, with no significant discordance identified. More specifically, the developed covariate model was used to support the current submission as outlined in Table 119.

L1659: ## 14.3.2. Introduction
L1660: The primary objectives of Applicant's popPK analyses were to:
L1661: - Develop a popPK model for bexagliflozin SR formulation and quantify individual PK parameters
- Evaluate the impact of clinical covariates on bexagliflozin PK
- Describe the unexplained variability in bexagliflozin PK
- Support dosing recommendations for bexagliflozin
L1662: Of note, the bexagliflozin clinical program also studied essential hypertension (b) (4) in two phase 3 trials, and subjects with essential hypertension (with or without T2DM) were included in the popPK dataset per the population PK analysis plan. Population type as a categorical variable was not included in the final popPK model (refer to Section 5.2 of Applicant's PopPK Report on covariate analysis). (b) (4)

L1682: ## Base Model
L1683: A base 2-compartment model with first-order [absorption (K_a) with lag time (T_{lag})] and first-order elimination (CL) was developed to characterize bexagliflozin disposition. A schematic of the base structural model is shown in Figure 37.
L1684: Interindividual variability (IIV) was modeled on primary PK parameters for patient level random effects in the base model. Residual variability was described using the proportional error model. Model selection from the base model was guided by change in objective function (OBJ), residual variance, IIV, and examination of diagnostic (e.g., goodness-of-fit) plots. Covariates for the final model were selected using the forward addition and backwards elimination approach using the base structural model.
L1685: **Figure 37. Scheme of Base Model Structure**
L1686: 1st order absorption (K_a) + lag-time model:
L1687: Source: Applicant's PopPK Report THR-1442-C-447, Figure S1, page 4
L1688: Abbreviations: CL, clearance; K_a, absorption constant; Q, inter-compartmental clearance; V_c, central volume of distribution; V_p, peripheral volume of distribution.
L1689: ***FDA Reviewer Comment:*** The Applicant also tested the same structural model with transit compartments and considered it a better base model (without covariates); however, the 2-compartment model with K_a and T_{lag} appeared to describe the pooled PK of bexagliflozin adequately via diagnostic plots (reviewer noted obvious trends for creatinine clearance [CrCL] and body weight when plotted against ETA for CL, indicating further model refinement was needed). As such, the Applicant noted that structural model with K_a and T_{lag} was used for covariate selection because of less computational intensity, and final covariate model refinement was conducted with the transit model.
L1690: ## Covariate Analysis
L1691: Covariates shown in Table 122 were evaluated in a forward-selection manner, and candidate models were evaluated based on OBJ reductions and PK parameter precision. The full model underwent backwards elimination. In addition, transit compartments were employed to describe the absorption profile as a candidate model, and an OMEGA block between CL and central compartment was also tested for the final covariate model. Refer to the Applicant's popPK report Section 5.2 for details on candidate models and results of backwards elimination.

L1735: ## 14.3.5. Reviewer's Independent Analysis
L1736: ## 14.3.5.1. Introduction
L1737: Trial C-449 was a phase 2b, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel group dose-ranging study in subjects with type 2 diabetes mellitus. The primary endpoint was to: 1) compare HbA1c reduction from baseline in treatment groups receiving 5 mg, 10 mg, or 20 mg
L1738: bexagliflozin to placebo group over 12 weeks, and 2) identify dose(s) for late-stage clinical trials. This analysis aims to describe the dose-response efficacy relationship (and the associated parameter variability) in T2DM subjects in Trial C-449.
L1739: ## 14.3.5.2. Objectives
L1740: Analysis objectives are:
L1741: - To identify the dose-response relationship of bexagliflozin
- To quantify the percent of pharmacological effect achieved with proposed dosage
L1742: ## 14.3.5.3. Methods
L1743: Analysis was conducted in R (version 3.6.3; R Core Team) and *DoseFinding*, an R package (Bjoern). After excluding the missing efficacy endpoints, a nonlinear model (dose-response E_{max} model) was fitted to the observed change in HbA1c (n=256) at Week 12 for the full analysis population using the *fitMod* function. Standard errors of the parameter estimates were used to generate the 95% confidence interval.
L1744: To obtain the placebo-adjusted percent of maximal pharmacological effect achieved at bexagliflozin 20 mg, a sensitivity analysis was conducted with placebo mean change set to zero. The analysis dataset is summarized in Table 125.
L1745: **Table 125. Analysis Dataset**
L1746: Trial Number	Name	Link to EDR
C-449	adeff.xpt	\CDSUB1\EVSPROD\nda214373\0001\m5\datasets\thr-1442-c-449\analysis\adam\datasets\adeff.xpt
L1747: Source: Submitted by Sponsor in NDA in Module 5.
L1748: ## 14.3.5.4. Results
L1749: After excluding missing data, 265 subjects were included in the analysis. Table 126 provides a summary of the sample size and efficacy endpoint for the analysis. Figure 45 illustrates the E_{max} model fit and the associated 95% CI based on parameter standard errors. The estimated half maximal effective dose was 2.96 mg (SE, 2.2) and E_{max} was -0.82% (SE, 0.16).

L1760: ## 14.4. Summary of Bioanalytical Method Validation and Performance
L1761: ## Bioanalytical Methods for the Measurement of Plasma Bexagliflozin
L1762: LC-MS/MS methods were developed and validated to determine concentrations of bexagliflozin and its metabolites in human plasma collected in the completed clinical studies. Detailed methods and validation parameters are described below (Table 128 to Table 132). The linearity of standard curve, selectivity/specificity, assay accuracy and precision, extraction efficiency, and dilution fulfilled the standard acceptance criteria. The established frozen storage stability and run storage stability covered the corresponding study period and sample analysis period. The reviewers deemed that these method validations and sample analyses are acceptable.
