L1777: ## 15.1.1. Clinical Protocol Synopsis for C-419 (Version 1.0, Date: July 26, 2017)
L1778: **Sponsor:** TheracosBio, LLC
L1779: **Name of Finished Product:** Bexagliflozin Tablet
L1780: **Name of Active Ingredient:** Bexagliflozin
L1781: **Study Title:** A Phase 3, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Study to Evaluate Bexagliflozin in Subjects with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Who Are not Adequately Controlled by Metformin Alone
L1782: **Study Number:** THR-1442-C-419
L1783: **Study Phase:** 3
L1784: **Primary Objective:** The primary objective of this study is to determine the effect of bexagliflozin on the placebo-corrected change in HbA1c from baseline to Week 24 in adults with T2DM whose disease is inadequately controlled by metformin alone.
L1785: **Secondary Objectives:**
L1786: - To assess the effect of bexagliflozin on the change in FPG as a function of time
- To assess the effect of bexagliflozin on the change in SBP as a function of time
L1787: - To assess the effect of bexagliflozin on the proportion of subjects achieving HbA1c of \le 7\% as a function of time
- To assess the change in total body weight as a function of time in subjects with baseline body mass index (BMI) \ge 25 kg/m^2
- To assess the change in HbA1c as a function of time
- To assess the change in HbA1c as a function of time among subjects who have baseline HbA1c of &gt;10.5\% and \le 12.0\%
L1788: **Study Design:** Trial C-419 is designed to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of bexagliflozin tablets, 20 mg, for the treatment of T2DM in adult diabetics whose disease is inadequately controlled by metformin alone. The study will recruit 300 subjects with HbA1c between 7.5% and 10.5%, inclusive, to be randomized 1:1 to receive bexagliflozin tablets, 20 mg, or placebo in a double-blind treatment assignment. The primary endpoint of the study will be the placebo-corrected change from baseline to Week 24 of the HbA1c percentage. This is the main study and these subjects are in the double-blind treatment group. The study will also recruit 50 subjects with HbA1c &gt;10.5\% and \le 12.0\% into an open-label arm, to receive bexagliflozin tablets, 20 mg, for 24 weeks. The endpoint for the open-label arm will be the change from baseline to Week 24 of the HbA1c percentage. These subjects are in the high glycemic group.
L1789: All subjects are to have taken metformin at an optimal or near optimal stable dose for \ge 8 weeks prior to screening and are to have received diet and exercise counseling. Subjects who meet all the inclusion criteria, none of the exclusion criteria, and who have consented to participate in the study, are eligible for study enrollment. Subjects who successfully complete a 1-week run-in and who remain eligible will be randomized.
L1790: Approximately 300 subjects with HbA1c values \ge 7.5 and \le 10.5\% at screening will be randomized 1:1 to receive bexagliflozin tablets, 20 mg, or placebo, in addition to their customary metformin dosage for 24 weeks in an outpatient setting. Study subjects will not change their metformin dosage unless adjustment is medically necessary to manage hypoglycemia. The treatment period will last 24 weeks. Subjects will visit their study sites at Weeks 6, 12, 18, and 24 for safety and efficacy evaluations, and at Week 26 for a follow-up evaluation.
L1791: Up to 50 subjects who have HbA1c &gt;10.5\% and \le 12.0\% at screening will be assigned to the open-label treatment group to receive bexagliflozin tablets, 20 mg, in addition to their existing metformin regimen. There will be no placebo arm for the high glycemic group. Subjects enrolled in the open label treatment group will be asked to follow the same procedures as subjects enrolled in the blinded arms of the study.
L1792: Subjects with persistent hyperglycemia based on blood glucose levels may receive approved antidiabetic rescue medications. A sparse sampling assessment of bexagliflozin PK in the study population will also be performed. A net enrollment of approximately 200 subjects is planned for this aspect of the study. Samples will be taken between Weeks 6 and 12. The population PK study design and analysis plan will be described in a designated study protocol and the analysis will be reported separately.
L1793: **Study Population:** Approximately 350 subjects with T2DM will be enrolled in the study. The subjects must:
L1794: (1) have an age of \ge 20 years at screening. Women of childbearing potential must test negative for pregnancy and agree to abstinence or contraception for the duration of the
L1795: study to avoid any possible pregnancy. Females who are surgically sterile (hysterectomy, oophorectomy) or postmenopausal (absence of menses greater than 12 months) are eligible if they test negative for pregnancy at screening.

- have a history of T2DM with an HbA1c level of \ge 7.5\% and \le 10.5\% at screening, or have a history of T2DM with an HbA1c level of &gt;10.5\% and \le 12.0\% at screening
- have been prescribed a stable dose of metformin (\ge 1500 mg per day in the US or \ge 1000 mg per day in Japan) as their sole anti-diabetic medication
- have a body mass index (BMI) \le 45 kg/m^2
- be able to comprehend and willing to provide written informed consent in accordance with institutional and regulatory guidelines
- not have recently changed their medications for hypertension or hyperlipidemia (if applicable)
- be able to regularly self-administer medication, as evidenced by consumption of all, or at worst one less than all, doses of run-in medication prior to randomization (at Visit 3)
L1796: **Test Product, Dose, and Mode of Administration:** Bexagliflozin tablets, 20 mg or placebo, once daily oral administration in 300 subjects Bexagliflozin tablets, 20 mg once daily oral administration in 50 subjects
L1797: **Duration of Treatment:** One week of run-in placebo treatment and 24 weeks of investigational product treatment
L1798: ## **Efficacy Assessments:**
L1799: The primary efficacy assessment is:
L1800: - The effect of bexagliflozin on the placebo-corrected change in HbA1c from baseline to Week 24 in adults with T2DM whose disease is inadequately controlled by metformin alone.
L1801: The key secondary efficacy assessments are:
L1802: - To assess the effect of bexagliflozin on the change in FPG as a function of time
- To assess the effect of bexagliflozin on the change in SBP as a function of time
- To assess the effect of bexagliflozin on the change in HbA1c as a function of time
- To assess the effect of bexagliflozin on the change in total body weight as a function of time in subjects with baseline BMI \ge 25 kg/m^2
- To assess the effect of bexagliflozin on the proportion of subjects achieving an HbA1c \le 7.0\% over time
- To assess the change in HbA1c as a function of time among subjects who have baseline HbA1c level of \ge 7.5\% and \le 10.5\%
- To measure the change from baseline to Week 24 in subjects with baseline HbA1c level of &gt;10.5\% and \le 12.0\%
L1803: **Other assessment:** Evaluation of bexagliflozin pharmacokinetics
L1804: **Safety Assessments:** Adverse events record, laboratory data including hematology, serum chemistry, urinalysis, electrocardiogram (ECG), vital signs, physical examinations, and concomitant medication use.
L1805: **Statistical Methods:** Summaries will be presented for double-blinded portion of the study, separately from the 50-subject open-label substudy. No formal hypothesis testing will be
L1806: performed for the substudy. Data summaries will report descriptive statistics (number of subjects [n], mean, SD, Q1, median, Q3, minimum, and maximum) for continuous variables, and frequency and percentage for categorical and ordinal variables.
L1807: The primary efficacy hypothesis is that bexagliflozin reduces HbA1c after 24 weeks of treatment when compared to placebo. The analysis of the change in HbA1c at Week 24 will be based on the intent-to-treat (ITT) analysis set using all observed data and an MMRM approach that will include terms for treatment, visit, treatment-by-visit interaction, baseline HbA1c value, and country (United States or Japan) as fixed effect covariates. Least squares mean treatment differences between the bexagliflozin group and the placebo group at Week 24 will be estimated from the model with the corresponding p-values and their two-sided 95% CIs presented. An unstructured covariance will be used to model the within-subject correlation. If the model with the unstructured covariance structure does not converge, an autoregressive covariance structure will be used. HbA1c values obtained after the start of rescue medication will not be excluded from the analysis.
L1808: The MMRM model is one approach to obtain treatment effect estimates in the presence of missing data. As sensitivity analyses for missing data, the following analysis steps will be performed on the ITT analysis set:
L1809: - Missing HbA1c data will be imputed via multiple imputations, following which the MMRM will be repeated on the complete datasets with results combined across complete datasets using standard multiple imputation techniques; HbA1c values collected after the start of rescue medication will not be excluded from the analysis.
- HbA1c values collected after the start of rescue medication will be excluded (considered missing), and the MMRM analyses will be reperformed.
- A last observation carried forward (LOCF) method will be used to impute the missing observations prior to carrying out the MMRM model.
L1810: The effect of bexagliflozin on fasting plasma glucose, the change in SBP, the proportion of subjects reaching \le 7.0\% HbA1c, the change in HbA1c over time, and the change in total body weight will be analyzed as secondary efficacy endpoints and will not be adjusted for multiplicity. Safety data will include adverse event (AE) descriptions, physical exam results, vital sign measurements, ECG results, and clinical lab results from analyses of serum chemistry, hematology, serum lipids, glycemic control parameters, and urinalysis. The general safety of bexagliflozin in subjects with type 2 diabetes mellitus will be analyzed as well as the contribution of bexagliflozin to AEs of special interest.
L1811: The sample size calculation for this study is based on two group t-test with a two-sided significance of 0.05 level. The assumptions that led to the estimated required sample size of 150 per group with 1:1 ratio for a power of 90% are as follows:
L1812: - A treatment effect of 0.4%.
- A population HbA1c standard deviation of 1%.
- A two-sided significance level of 0.05.
- A drop-out rate of 12%.
L1813: ***FDA Reviewer Comment:*** *Metformin is the most commonly prescribed oral antihyperglycemic agent for T2DM and is often recommended as a first-line therapy for the treatment of T2DM. The study was conducted in the United States and Japan, and stratification by country (United*
L1814: *States versus Japan) and baseline HbA1c status (\le 8.5\% versus &gt;8.5\%) was performed. The protocol was similar to other protocols reviewed in the Division; however, it is noteworthy that subjects were eligible for enrollment at Japanese sites if on stable metformin doses \ge 1,000 mg metformin per day (as opposed to \ge 1500 mg per day, which is a commonly used threshold in other programs and was used at US-based sites in this trial). However, this would not be expected to change the overall conclusions from the study.*
L1815: *With regards to trial conduct, there were no amendments to Version 1 and the only modifications to the protocol were regarding planned analyses. Investigators were trained on the study protocol and procedures during site initiation meetings. Each center was visited at regular intervals by a monitor to ensure compliance with the study protocol, good clinical practice (GCP) guidelines, and the law. This included on-site checking of the CRFs for completeness and clarity, verification with source documents, and clarification of administrative matters. Seven site audits were conducted during the trial. One critical finding, regarding lack of review of laboratory results by the investigator within 3 days of receipt, was found at a US clinical site. The investigator was retrained on review of laboratory reports, GCP, and site SOPs. This finding is unlikely to impact trial outcomes.*
L1816: *There were 14 (8.9%) and 11 (6.9%) subjects with at least one major protocol violation/deviation in the bexagliflozin and placebo groups, respectively. The majority of protocol deviations in both treatment groups were “IP not taken as per protocol” and “noncompliance with visit schedule.” The number of protocol deviations/violations was low and was generally consistent between treatment groups.*
L1817: *Overall, the protocol is generally similar to other protocols reviewed in the Division to evaluate the impact of SGLT2 inhibitor treatment on glycemic control in subjects on metformin monotherapy, and the trial appears to have been conducted adequately.*
L1818: ## **15.1.2. Clinical Protocol Synopsis for C-423 (Version 2.0, Date: April 06, 2017)**
L1819: **Sponsor:** TheracosBio, LLC
L1820: **Name of Finished Product:** Bexagliflozin Tablets
L1821: **Name of Active Ingredient:** Bexagliflozin
L1822: **Study Title:** A Phase 3, Randomized, Double-Blind, Active-Controlled Study to Evaluate the Effects of Bexagliflozin Versus Sitagliptin in Subjects with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Who Have Inadequate Glycemic Control by Metformin
L1823: **Study Number:** THR-1442-C-423
L1824: **Study Phase:** 3
L1825: **Primary Objective:** The primary efficacy objective is to demonstrate that bexagliflozin is noninferior to sitagliptin by evaluating the treatment effect on hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) reduction at Week 24 in subjects whose T2DM is inadequately controlled by metformin.
L1826: **Secondary Objectives:** The key secondary objectives are:
L1827: - To evaluate the treatment effect of bexagliflozin versus sitagliptin on the change in FPG at Week 24
- To evaluate the treatment effect of bexagliflozin versus sitagliptin on the change in body weight in subjects with baseline BMI \ge 25 kg/m^2 at Week 24
- To evaluate the treatment effect of bexagliflozin versus sitagliptin on the change in SBP in subjects at Week 24
L1828: **Exploratory Objectives:**
L1829: - To assess the treatment effect of bexagliflozin versus sitagliptin on the change in the proportion of subjects achieving HbA1c &lt;7.0% over time
- To assess the treatment effect of bexagliflozin versus sitagliptin on the change in HbA1c over time
- To assess the treatment effect of bexagliflozin versus sitagliptin on the change in FPG over time
- To assess the treatment effect of bexagliflozin versus sitagliptin on the change in body weight over time
- To assess the treatment effect of bexagliflozin versus sitagliptin on the change in SBP over time
L1830: **Safety Objectives:** To compare the effects of bexagliflozin with sitagliptin on the incidence of AEs of interest. AEs of interest are urinary tract infections (UTIs), urosepsis and pyelonephritis, genital mycotic infections (GMI), diuretic effects including hypovolemia, hypotension episodes, hypoglycemia, hepatotoxicity, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), falls and fractures, malignancies, hypersensitivity reactions, acid-base disorders including DKA, pancreatitis, amputations, and renal failure events. To compare the effects of bexagliflozin with sitagliptin on general safety assessments including treatment-emergent AEs, clinical laboratory findings, 12-lead ECG parameters, physical examinations, vital signs including orthostatic blood pressure (BP), and use of concomitant medications.
L1831: **Study Design:** C-423 is a phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, active controlled study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of bexagliflozin versus sitagliptin in subjects whose T2DM is not well controlled by metformin alone. A total of 374 subjects are planned to be randomized in a ratio of 1:1 to receive once daily treatment of bexagliflozin tablets, 20 mg, with sitagliptin tablets, placebo (Group 1) or bexagliflozin tablets, placebo, with sitagliptin tablets, 100 mg (Group 2) for 24 weeks in an outpatient setting.
L1832: The main eligibility criteria include 1) male or female subjects with T2DM and 2) screening HbA1c between 7.0% and 11% (inclusive). Qualified subjects must have taken metformin at a stable dose of \ge 1500 mg/day in addition to diet and exercise counseling for at least 8 weeks prior to screening. Study subjects will continue taking open-labeled metformin during the entire study. All eligible subjects will start a single-blind run-in period by taking placebo bexagliflozin and placebo sitagliptin once daily for one week. Subjects who meet all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria after completion of the run-in period will be eligible for randomization and receive investigational products.
L1833: During the treatment period, subjects will receive once daily sitagliptin tablets, 100 mg, and bexagliflozin tablets, placebo, or bexagliflozin tablets, 20 mg, and sitagliptin tablets, placebo, for
L1834: 24 weeks. Each subject will be instructed to return to the clinic at Weeks 6, 12, 18, and 24 for efficacy assessment and safety monitoring. Subjects will return to the clinic for a follow-up exit visit at Week 26 or 2 weeks after last dose of study drug if subjects early terminate prior to Week 24. During the study, a data and safety monitoring board (DSMB) will review the unblinded data periodically and may recommend an early termination of the trial for safety reasons. In the event of administrative changes or other related reasons, the Sponsor reserves the right to terminate the study early. There will be no interim analysis; final statistical analysis will be performed after all subjects complete the study.
L1835: **Study Population and Main Eligibility Criteria:** A total of 374 eligible subjects are planned for this study. The study population will comprise:
L1836: - Male or female adult subjects \ge 18 years of age
- If subjects are female of childbearing potential, subjects must be negative on the urine pregnancy test and agree to abstain from coitus or use contraception during the entire study to avoid any possible pregnancy
- Subjects with a diagnosis of T2DM with HbA1c levels between 7.0% and 11% (inclusive) at screening
- Subjects whose T2DM is treated with a stable dose of \ge 1500 mg/day metformin only along with diet and exercise counseling for at least 8 weeks prior to screening
- Subjects with a BMI \le 45 kg/m^2 at screening
- If applicable, taking stable doses of treatment for dyslipidemia and/or hypertension for 30 days prior to screening. Subjects do not need to be treated for dyslipidemia or hypertension to be eligible for the study
- Subjects who are willing and able to return for all clinic visits and to complete all study-required procedures, including self-monitoring blood glucose (SMBG) measurements
L1837: Prior to randomization, all subjects must:
L1838: - Adhere to the investigational product administration requirements as evidenced by missing no more than 1 day of placebo run-in medication
L1839: ## **Test Products, Dose, and Mode of Administration:**
L1840: Once daily oral administration of bexagliflozin and sitagliptin with or without food taken together in the morning
L1841: - Group 1: bexagliflozin tablets, 20 mg, and sitagliptin tablets, placebo
- Group 2: bexagliflozin tablets, placebo, and sitagliptin tablets, 100 mg
L1842: **Duration of Treatment:** Eligible subjects will receive a total treatment duration of 25 weeks including 1 week of run-in medications and 24 weeks of investigational products.
L1843: ## **Efficacy Assessments:**
L1844: Primary efficacy assessment:
L1845: - Change in HbA1c from baseline at Week 24
L1846: ## Secondary efficacy assessments:
L1847: - Change in FPG from baseline at Week 24
- Change in body weight in subjects with baseline BMI \ge 25 kg/m^2 at Week 24
- Change in SBP in subjects from baseline at Week 24
L1848: ## Other efficacy endpoints:
L1849: - To assess the treatment effect of bexagliflozin versus sitagliptin on the change in the proportion of subjects achieving HbA1c &lt;7.0% over time
- To assess the treatment effect of bexagliflozin versus sitagliptin on the change in HbA1c over time
- To assess the treatment effect of bexagliflozin versus sitagliptin on the change in FPG over time
- To assess the treatment effect of bexagliflozin versus sitagliptin on the change in body weight over time
- To assess the treatment effect of bexagliflozin versus sitagliptin on the change in SBP over time
L1850: ## Safety endpoints:
L1851: - Treatment-emergent AEs, including AESIs (genital and urinary tract infections, diuretic effects, hepatotoxicity, MACE, hypoglycemia, fractures, malignancy, hypersensitivity reactions, hypotensive episodes, acid-base disorders, pancreatitis, amputations, and renal failure events)
- Laboratory testing, including hematology, serum chemistry, and urinalysis
- Physical examination
- 12-lead ECG
- Vital signs
- Concomitant medication use
L1852: **Statistical Methods:** The primary hypothesis is that bexagliflozin is noninferior to sitagliptin by evaluating the treatment effect on HbA1c reduction at Week 24 in combination with metformin. The noninferiority margin for mean change from baseline at Week 24 in HbA1c comparing bexagliflozin group with sitagliptin group will be 0.35%. Superiority will be declared without additional statistical testing when the upper bound of the 95% CI for difference in change from baseline at Week 24 in HbA1c comparing bexagliflozin group with sitagliptin group is less than 0. The treatment difference will be examined by using an MMRM analysis of covariance model (ANCOVA). The model will include treatment, visit, treatment-by-visit interaction, region, and the baseline HbA1c value as fixed effect covariates. Least squares mean treatment differences between the bexagliflozin group and the comparator group at Week 24 in change from baseline will be estimated from the model. An unstructured covariance will be used to model the within-subject correlation. If the model with the unstructured covariance structure does not converge, an autoregressive (1) covariance structure will be used. HbA1c values obtained after the start of rescue medication will not be excluded from this primary analysis. Primary endpoints will be analyzed on both ITT and per protocol (PP) analysis sets.
L1853: The MMRM model is one approach to obtain treatment effect estimates in the presence of missing data. As sensitivity analyses for missing data, the following will be performed on both ITT and PP analysis sets:
L1854: - Missing data will be imputed via multiple imputations, following which the MMRM will be repeated on the complete datasets with results combined across complete datasets using standard multiple imputation techniques; HbA1c values collected after the start of rescue medication will be excluded.
- Missing data will be imputed via LOCF, following which the MMRM will be repeated; HbA1c values collected after the start of rescue medication will be considered missing.
- HbA1c values collected after the start of rescue medication will be considered missing, and the MMRM analyses will be reperformed.
L1855: The effects of bexagliflozin on the changes from baseline at Week 24 in FPG, body weight, and SBP will be tested as key secondary endpoints and will be analyzed in a hierarchical testing strategy and only if the primary objective is met. Similar to the primary endpoint, MMRM ANCOVA models will be used. A hierarchical testing strategy will be followed to preserve experiment-wide alpha at 0.05:
L1856: - Superiority test of the change in FPG in the bexagliflozin group versus the sitagliptin group at Week 24
- Superiority test of the change in body weight in subjects with baseline BMI \ge 25 kg/m^2 in the bexagliflozin group versus the sitagliptin group at Week 24
- Superiority test of the change in SBP in the bexagliflozin group versus the sitagliptin group at Week 24
L1857: Additional effects of bexagliflozin versus sitagliptin on the changes in HbA1c, FPG, SBP, body weight, and the proportion of subjects who reach an HbA1c &lt;7%, as well as the general safety in subjects with T2DM, will be analyzed as exploratory efficacy endpoints. These endpoints are considered exploratory and will not be adjusted for multiplicity.
L1858: For the primary efficacy endpoint, a minimum of 172 subjects are needed in each treatment arm to detect noninferiority of bexagliflozin to sitagliptin with respect to the change in HbA1c from baseline at Week 24 by a margin of 0.35%, assuming an estimated pooled SD of 1.0%. This estimation is based on a one-sided t-test with 90% power at a 0.025 level of significance. To allow for an estimated 8.0% dropout rate, 187 patients will be randomized in each treatment arm, and the total sample size will be 374 subjects for this study.
L1859: Statistical analyses and summaries will be performed using SAS® software (SAS Institute, Cary, NC).
L1860: Date of Protocol V2.0: April 6, 2017
L1861: Date of Protocol V1.0: February 1, 2017
L1862: ***FDA Reviewer Comment:*** *This study was intended to evaluate whether bexagliflozin is noninferior compared to another antihyperglycemic agent (sitagliptin) commonly prescribed as add-on for patients failing to achieve glycemic goals on metformin. Sitagliptin was used at the recommended dosage strength for patients without renal impairment (i.e., 100 mg), which is appropriate for this study design to ensure that NI is not resultant from suboptimal dosing in the active comparator arm. The protocol is similar to other protocols reviewed in the Division,*
L1863: *although the NI margin was larger than what has been used in other SGLT2 inhibitor development programs (i.e., 0.35% as opposed to 0.3%). At the IND stage, FDA agreed with the margin selection and accepted the Applicant's justification for the proposed margin.*
L1864: *Protocol version 2.0 was the only protocol used in the study. Each center was visited at regular intervals by a monitor to ensure compliance with the study protocol, GCP, and legal aspects. A clinical site audit was conducted at investigational site 1271 on December 11, 2017. Major findings in GCP conduct included performing prescreening activities prior to subjects providing written informed consent for the study, lack of appropriate participation and oversight by the investigator, and failure of the investigator to provide adequate and accurate case histories for subjects treated in the study. Based on these findings, the Applicant decided to discontinue the investigator's participation of the study on March 22, 2018. Seven subjects had completed screening procedures and two subjects, one assigned to the bexagliflozin group and one assigned to the active-comparator group, were enrolled and received double blind investigational products for 6 to 12 weeks. Data of the two enrolled subjects were excluded from the ITT and safety analysis sets. Exclusion of these two subjects from the ITT would not be expected to change efficacy conclusions from the trial.*
L1865: *Protocol deviations were reported for 9 (4.7%) and 8 (4.1%) of subjects in the bexagliflozin and placebo groups, respectively. The number of protocol deviations was low and consistent between treatment groups.*
L1866: *Overall, the study appears adequately designed and conducted.*
L1867: ## 15.1.3. Clinical Protocol Synopsis for C-448 (Version 4.0, Date: October 25, 2016)
L1868: **Sponsor:** TheracosBio, LLC
L1869: **Name of Finished Product:** Bexagliflozin Tablets
L1870: **Name of Active Ingredient:** Bexagliflozin
L1871: **Study Title:** A Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Study to Evaluate the Effect of Bexagliflozin Tablets on Hemoglobin A1c in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Moderate Renal Impairment
L1872: **Study Number:** THR-1442-C-448
L1873: **Study Phase:** 3
L1874: **Primary Objective:** The primary objective of this study is to determine the efficacy of bexagliflozin on lowering HbA1c in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and moderate renal impairment.
L1875: **Secondary Objectives:** The key secondary efficacy objectives are:
L1876: - To assess the effect of bexagliflozin on the change in body weight at Week 24 in subjects with baseline BMI \ge 25 \text{ kg/m}^2
- To assess the effect of bexagliflozin on the change in SBP at Week 24 in subjects with baseline SBP \ge 130 \text{ mm Hg}
L1877: - Change in HbA1c in subjects with estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) 45 to 59 mL/min/1.73 m2 at Week 24
- Change in HbA1c in subjects with eGFR 30 to 44 mL/min/1.73 m2 at Week 24
L1878: **Study Design:** C-448 is a phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of oral administration of bexagliflozin tablets, 20 mg compared to placebo in subjects with T2DM, moderate renal impairment, and inadequate glycemic control. Main eligibility criteria include: 1) male or female subjects with T2DM, 2) screening HbA1c of 7.0 to 10.5% (inclusive), and 3) eGFR based on serum creatinine at 2 different assessments \ge 30 to &lt;60 mL/min/1.73 m2. The eGFR will be calculated by the modification of diet in renal disease study equation (MDRD). At the time of screening, the doses and frequency of all antidiabetic medications must have been stable for 8 weeks.
L1879: All eligible subjects will continue their prescreening antidiabetic medications and start a 1-week placebo run-in period. Subjects who are compliant in taking run-in medication (missing no more than one dose) will be eligible for randomization and receive study drug. Approximately 300 subjects (150 per arm) will be randomly assigned to receive bexagliflozin tablets, 20 mg or placebo, in equal ratio once daily for 24 weeks in an outpatient setting. Randomization will be stratified by screening HbA1c level (7.0 to 8.5% or 8.6 to 10.5%), screening antidiabetic treatment regimen (insulin treated or other) and screening eGFR (30 to 44 mL/min/1.73 m2 or 45 to 59 mL/min/1.73 m2). A minimum of 135 subjects must be in the eGFR 30 to 44 mL/min/1.73 m2 stratum.
L1880: Subjects with hyperglycemia based on blood glucose levels may receive approved antidiabetic medication. In addition, adjustment by the investigator to the prescreening antidiabetic therapies will be recommended if hypoglycemia occurs. Study subjects will have scheduled visits at Weeks 2, 6, 12, 18, and 24 for safety and efficacy evaluation. At Weeks 2 and 18, the visit will be conducted by a phone interview unless clinically necessary. A final follow-up visit will be conducted at Week 26. Measurement of bexagliflozin plasma concentration over time (sparsely sampled) will also be conducted from approximately 144 study subjects as part of a bexagliflozin popPK study.
L1881: **Study Population:** The study population will consist of 300 subjects who have been diagnosed with suboptimally controlled T2DM with moderate renal impairment. The study population will comprise:
L1882: - Men or nonpregnant women \ge 20 years of age. Women of childbearing potential must agree to use contraception during the entire study to avoid any possible pregnancy. Females who are surgically sterile (hysterectomy, oophorectomy) or postmenopausal (absence of menses greater than 12 months and age &gt;45 years) are eligible if they test negative on the urine pregnancy test.
- Subjects with a diagnosis of T2DM with an HbA1c between 7.0 and 10.5% (inclusive) at the time of screening.
- Subjects who are treatment naïve or are treated with a stable regimen of anti-diabetic medications that do not provide adequate glycemic control when combined with diet and exercise. At the time of screening, the doses and frequency of all anti-diabetic medications must have been stable for 8 weeks.
- Subjects who have an eGFR \ge 30 and &lt;60 mL/min/1.73 m2 at 2 time points: screening (V1), and 1 additional time point between 1 and 12 months of screening (the most recent
L1883: historical value may be obtained from available medical records). The eGFR will be calculated by the MDRD equation.
L1884: - Subjects who have a BMI \le 45 \text{ kg/m}^2 (inclusive)
- Subjects taking stable doses of medications for hypertension or hyperlipidemia for at least 30 days prior to randomization
- Subjects who have stable eGFR between the most recent historic value and day of screening (no more than 20% change in eGFR).
L1885: **Test Product, Dose, and Mode of Administration:** Bexagliflozin tablets, 20 mg or placebo, once daily by mouth
L1886: **Duration of Treatment:** 25 weeks: 1 week run-in, 24 weeks of treatment
L1887: ## **Efficacy Assessments:**
L1888: Primary efficacy assessment:
L1889: - Change of HbA1c from baseline to Week 24
L1890: Secondary efficacy assessments:
L1891: - Change in body weight in subjects with baseline BMI \ge 25 \text{ kg/m}
- Changes in SBP over time in subjects with baseline SBP \ge 130 \text{ mm Hg}
- Change in HbA1c over time in subjects with eGFR 45 to 59 mL/min/1.73 \text{m}^2
- Change in HbA1c over time in subjects with eGFR 30 to 44 mL/min/1.73 \text{m}^2
- Samples for population PK analysis will be collected and the required plasma concentrations determined. The PK parameters will be assessed separately as part of the population PK analysis.
L1892: **Safety Assessments:** Safety will be assessed based on an analysis of the adverse events record; of laboratory data, including hematology, serum chemistry, urinalysis, urinary electrolytes, and creatinine; of ECGs, vital signs and physical examinations; and of concomitant medication use.
L1893: **Statistical Methods:** In general, descriptive statistics will be presented for continuous variables, and frequency and percentage for categorical variables.
L1894: For the primary objectives, efficacy is defined as lowering of HbA1c at Week 24 from baseline for bexagliflozin when compared to placebo. For the primary endpoint analysis, the primary analysis will utilize an MMRM ANCOVA approach, with treatment, visit, treatment-by-visit interaction, and randomization stratification factors as the fixed effects terms and baseline HbA1c as a covariate on all available data, incorporating all visits from each patient at which HbA1c was measured in the ITT analysis set. All observed data will be analyzed and data obtained after rescue will not be excluded. In addition, same analyses will be conducted in PP analysis set (if it is deemed different from the ITT analysis set).
L1895: The MMRM model is one approach to obtain treatment effect estimates in the presence of missing data. As sensitivity analyses for missing data, the following will be performed for the ITT analysis set:
L1896: - Missing HbA1c data will be imputed via multiple imputation, following which the MMRM will be repeated on the complete datasets with results combined across complete datasets using standard multiple imputation techniques; HbA1c values collected after the start of rescue medication will not be excluded.
L1897: (2) Missing HbA1c data will be imputed via LOCF, following which the MMRM will be repeated; HbA1c values collected after the start of rescue medication will be considered missing.

(3) HbA1c values collected after the start of rescue medication will be considered missing, and the MMRM analyses will be reperformed.
L1898: If the PP analysis set is different from the ITT analysis set, the same analyses as described above will be conducted in PP analysis set as well.
L1899: The effects of bexagliflozin on the secondary endpoints will be tested in a hierarchical testing strategy to preserve experiment-wide type I error at 0.05:
L1900: (1) Superiority test of the change in body weight in subjects with baseline BMI \ge 25 kg/m^2 in the bexagliflozin group compared to the placebo group

(2) Superiority test of the change in SBP over time in subjects with SBP \ge 130 mm Hg in the bexagliflozin group compared to the placebo group

(3) Superiority test of the change in HbA1c over time in subjects with eGFR 45 to 59 mL/min/1.73m^2 in the bexagliflozin group compared to the placebo group

(4) Superiority test of the change in HbA1c over time in subjects with eGFR 30 to 44 mL/min/1.73m^2 in the bexagliflozin group compared to the placebo group
L1901: Additional effects of bexagliflozin on FPG, changes in HbA1c over time, proportion of subjects who reach an HbA1c &lt;7%, change in body weight over time, change in urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) over time, and the general safety of bexagliflozin in subjects with T2DM will be analyzed. No hypothesis testing will be conducted and will not be adjusted for multiplicity.
L1902: For the primary efficacy endpoint, sample size calculation is based on a two-sided significance at the 5% level. Assuming 1.0% as the standard deviation for difference in mean changes from baseline in HbA1c between bexagliflozin and placebo, an estimated sample size of 133 in each arm will have 90% power to detect a difference in mean HbA1c changes of 0.40% between bexagliflozin and placebo. To account for an estimated dropout rate of 12%, we propose randomizing 150 subjects in each study arm.
L1903: Statistical analyses and summaries will be performed using SAS software (SAS Institute, Cary, NC).
L1904: ***FDA Reviewer Comment:*** This trial evaluated the use of bexagliflozin as add-on to standard of care (i.e., not as monotherapy or add-on to metformin) in subjects with T2DM and moderate renal impairment failing standard of care antihyperglycemic therapy, which is a patient population for whom an SGLT2 inhibitor would be added in clinical practice. Considering the variability of eGFR measurements, randomization of subjects based on a single laboratory assessment could result in inclusion of participants with an eGFR less than or greater than the desired eGFR criteria. To identify subjects with moderate renal impairment, the protocol specified that subject must have screening eGFR \ge 30 and &lt;60 mL/min/1.73 m^2 and stable GFR (no more than 20% change in eGFR between a historical value and the value determined at the screening visit). Randomization was stratified by HbA1c level (\ge 7.0 to &lt;8.5% versus \ge 8.5 to &lt;10.5%), antidiabetic treatment regimen (with insulin or without), and eGFR (30 to 44 mL/min/1.73 m^2 versus 45 to 59 mL/min/1.73 m^2). In general, the protocol is similar to others reviewed in the Division to assess efficacy and safety of SGLT2 inhibitor treatment in subjects
L1905: with renal impairment, although it is noteworthy that studies differ with regards to the specific populations being enrolled (e.g., evaluation only in subjects with stage 3a chronic kidney disease (CKD) versus stage 3a and 3b CKD). The degree of renal impairment and other comorbidities may be expected to impact study results, and thus, cross-study comparisons are inadvisable.
L1906: Updates to the protocol from Version 3, which was the first version under which subjects were enrolled, to Version 4 were generally minor (e.g., addition of amputation as an AESI, clarification of selected inclusion criteria). There were 13 (8.3%) and 12 (7.7%) subjects in the bexagliflozin group and placebo groups that had at least one major protocol deviation, respectively. The number of protocol deviations were low and generally balanced between treatment arms. Overall, the trial design, enrolled population, and treatment duration were adequate and generally consistent with trials submitted to the Division to inform labeling in this patient population.
L1907: ## 15.1.4. Clinical Protocol Synopsis for C-450 (Version 4.0, Date: April 04, 2017)
L1908: **Sponsor:** TheracosBio, LLC
L1909: **Name of Finished Product:** Bexagliflozin Tablets
L1910: **Name of Active Ingredient:** Bexagliflozin
L1911: **Study Title:** A Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Parallel Group Study to Compare the Efficacy and Safety of Bexagliflozin to Placebo in Subjects With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Inadequate Glycemic Control
L1912: **Study Number:** THR-1442-C-450
L1913: **Study Phase:** 3
L1914: **Primary Objective:** To determine the placebo-adjusted treatment effect of bexagliflozin tablets, 20 mg on the change in HbA1c from baseline to Week 24 in subjects with type 2 diabetes mellitus and inadequate glycemic control.
L1915: ## **Key Secondary Objectives:**
L1916: - To assess the effect of bexagliflozin on systolic blood pressure compared to placebo
- To assess the effect of bexagliflozin on body weight in subjects with a baseline BMI \ge 25 \text{ kg/m}^2 compared to placebo
L1917: ## **Exploratory Secondary Objectives**
L1918: - To compare the effect of bexagliflozin to the effect of placebo on the proportion of subjects with HbA1c of &lt;7%
- To compare the effect of bexagliflozin to the effect of placebo on change in HbA1c over time
- To compare the effect of bexagliflozin to the effect of placebo on FPG over time
L1919: ## **Safety Objectives:**
L1920: - To assess the safety of bexagliflozin in subjects with T2DM
- To assess the effect of bexagliflozin on the incidence of AESIs
L1921: - To contribute MACE+ events to an eventual meta-analysis that is intended to exclude a hazard ratio of 1.8 or greater for subjects exposed to bexagliflozin compared to subjects exposed to placebo or comparator treatment
L1922: **Study Design:** C-450 is a phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of once daily oral administration of bexagliflozin tablets, 20 mg, versus placebo in subjects with T2DM who are treatment-naïve or previously treated with one oral hypoglycemic agent (OHA).
L1923: The study will enroll male or female subjects with T2DM. If treatment-naïve, they must have an HbA1c at the screening visit of between 7% and 10.5%. Alternatively, prospective subjects may be eligible if at the time of the screening visit, they are being treated with one OHA, have an HbA1c of between 6.5% and 10.0%, and are willing to complete a 6-week washout. Individuals taking thiazolidinediones are not eligible for the study. A candidate will be considered treatment-naïve if they have received no more than 14 days of prescription medication for diabetes in the 12 weeks prior to screening. All eligible subjects will start a 2-week placebo run-in period. Subjects who miss no more than one dose of the run-in medication, have fasting blood glucose values \ge 250 mg/dL on no more than two consecutive days, and who, at the baseline visit (Visit V5), have an HbA1c level between 7 and 10.5% and a fasting glucose level &lt;250 mg/dL will be eligible for randomization.
L1924: Approximately 210 subjects will be randomly assigned to receive oral bexagliflozin tablets, 20 mg, or placebo in a 2:1 ratio once daily for 24 weeks in an out-patient setting. Subjects with uncontrolled hyperglycemia based on blood glucose levels may receive additional approved antidiabetic medications. Treatment group assignment at the start of the treatment period will be stratified by baseline (Visit V5) HbA1c level (7.0 to 8.5% or 8.6 to 10.5%) and background antidiabetic treatment status (treatment-naïve or not). Each subject will be contacted by telephone at Week 2 (Visit V7) for safety monitoring and will be instructed to return to the clinic at Weeks 6, 12, 18, and 24 (Visits V8, V9, V10, and V11, respectively) for efficacy assessment and safety monitoring. Subjects will return to the clinic for a follow-up visit at Week 26 or two weeks after the last dose of investigational product if the subject terminates prior to Week 24 (Visit V12).
L1925: **Study Population and Main Eligibility Criteria:** Approximately 210 subjects are planned for this study. The study will enroll:
L1926: - Male or female adult subjects \ge 18 years of age at screening.
- Subjects with T2DM who are treatment-naïve or receiving one OHA in combination with diet and exercise. Subjects taking thiazolidinediones are not eligible.
- Subjects with HbA1c levels at screening (Visit V1) between 7.0% and 10.5% (inclusive) if treatment-naïve or with HbA1c levels between 6.5 and 10.0% (inclusive) if on one OHA
- Subjects with a BMI \le 45 kg/m^2
- Subjects with a fasting plasma glucose &lt;250 mg/dL (13.9 mmol/L) at baseline (Visit V5)
L1927: **Test Product, Dose, and Mode of Administration:** Bexagliflozin tablets, 20 mg, or placebo administered orally once daily
L1928: **Duration of Treatment:** 24 weeks
L1929: **Efficacy Assessments:** The primary efficacy measure will be the change in HbA1c from baseline to Week 24. The key secondary measures will be the changes from baseline to Week 24 of systolic blood pressure and body weight. The exploratory secondary measures will be the change from baseline of the fasting plasma glucose concentration over time, the change from baseline of HbA1c over time, and the proportion of subjects who achieve an HbA1c &lt;7% over time.
L1930: **Safety Assessments:** The safety of bexagliflozin will be assessed over the 24-week treatment phase. AEs of special interest include genital and urinary tract infections, diuretic effects, hepatotoxicity, MACE, hypoglycemia, fractures, malignancy, hypersensitivity reactions, hypotensive episodes, acid-base disorders, renal failure events, and amputations.
L1931: **Statistical Methods:** Data summaries will report descriptive statistics (number of subjects [n], mean, SD, Q1, median, Q3, minimum, and maximum for continuous variables, and frequency and percentage for categorical and ordinal variables). If there are missing values, the number missing will be presented, but without a percentage. All data collected will be included in by-subject data listings.
L1932: The primary efficacy hypothesis is that bexagliflozin reduces HbA1c after 24 weeks of treatment when compared to placebo. The analysis of the change in HbA1c at Week 24 will be based on ITT analysis set using all observed data and an MMRM approach that will include terms for treatment, visit, treatment-by-visit interaction, and randomization stratification factors as fixed effects and the baseline HbA1c value as a fixed effect covariate. Least squares mean treatment differences between the bexagliflozin group and the placebo group at Week 24 will be estimated from the model with the corresponding p-values and their two-sided 95% CI presented. An unstructured covariance will be used to model the within-subject correlation. If the model with the unstructured covariance structure does not converge, an autoregressive (1) covariance structure will be used. HbA1c values obtained after the start of rescue medication will not be excluded from the analysis.
L1933: The MMRM model is one approach to obtain treatment effect estimates in the presence of missing data. As sensitivity analyses for missing data, the following will be performed on the ITT analysis set:
L1934: - Missing HbA1c data will be imputed via multiple imputations, following which the MMRM will be repeated on the complete datasets with results combined across complete datasets using standard multiple imputation techniques; HbA1c values collected after the start of rescue medication will not be excluded from the analysis.
- HbA1c values collected after the start of rescue medication will be excluded (considered missing), and the MMRM analyses will be reperformed.
- An LOCF method will then be used to impute the missing observations prior to carrying out the MMRM model.
L1935: The effect of bexagliflozin on body weight and systolic blood pressure will be tested as key secondary efficacy endpoints and will be analyzed in a hierarchical testing strategy only if the primary objective is met. ANCOVA models will also be used for the continuous secondary endpoints analyses. Longitudinal data will be evaluated through repeated measures tests. A
L1936: hierarchical testing in the following order will be applied to preserve experiment-wide alpha at 0.05 in the case each successive determination meets significance:
L1937: - To test the hypothesis that bexagliflozin reduces systolic blood pressure from baseline to Week 24 compared with placebo
- To test the hypothesis that bexagliflozin reduces body weight from baseline to Week 24 compared with placebo in subjects with a BMI \ge 25 \text{ kg/m}^2
L1938: The effect of bexagliflozin on fasting plasma glucose, on the proportion of subjects reaching &lt;7.0\% \text{ HbA1c}, and on the change in HbA1c over time will be analyzed as exploratory efficacy endpoints and will not be adjusted for multiplicity.
L1939: Safety data will include AEs, physical exam results, vital signs, ECG results, and clinical lab results including serum chemistry, hematology, serum lipids, glycemic control parameters and urinalysis. The general safety of bexagliflozin in subjects with type 2 diabetes mellitus will be analyzed as well as the contribution of bexagliflozin to AEs of special interest.
L1940: For the primary efficacy endpoint, a power calculation was performed for significance calculated by a two-group t-test with a two-sided \alpha of 0.05. Taking the standard deviation for the change in HbA1c to be 1%, a sample size of 128 in the bexagliflozin group and 64 in the placebo group is predicted to have 90% power to detect a difference between groups of 0.5% in mean HbA1c change. To account for an estimated drop-out rate of approximately 10%, a study design was adopted in which 140 subjects are planned to be randomized to the bexagliflozin group and 70 subjects to the placebo group. Statistical analyses and summaries will be performed using SAS software (SAS Institute, Cary, NC).
L1941: ***FDA Reviewer Comment:*** *This trial evaluated the effect of bexagliflozin on HbA1c in treatment-naïve subjects with T2DM or who were on one OHA and had inadequate glycemic control. Subjects were considered treatment-naïve if they had received no more than 14 days of prescription medication for diabetes in the 12 weeks prior to screening. In addition, subjects were considered treatment-naïve if taking one oral antihyperglycemic agent and willing to undergo a 6-week washout period prior to randomization. All subjects were required to undergo a 2-week placebo run-in period. Therefore, subjects on one oral antihyperglycemic agent would have been without diabetes management therapy for a minimum of 8 weeks prior to administration of the investigational product. Randomization was stratified by HbA1c (7.0 to 8.5% or 8.6 to 10.5%) and background antidiabetic treatment status (treatment-naïve or not). These procedures appear reasonable to include subjects previously taking one oral antihyperglycemic agent in the trial.*
L1942: *The original protocol (Version 2.1) was dated February 10, 2016. Minor changes were made to the protocol in Version 3 (change of medical monitor/study statistician, addition of amputation as an AESI) and Version 4 (subsequent change of study statistician and updates to analysis plan). There were 36 (26.1%) and 12 (17.4%) of subjects with at least one major protocol deviation in the bexagliflozin and placebo groups, respectively. In both groups, the majority of protocol deviations were “noncompliance with visit schedule.” Three randomized subjects, two in the bexagliflozin group and one in the placebo group, were excluded from the ITT population due to protocol violations. Subject 450 (b) (6) and Subject 450 (b) (6) were the same person who enrolled in two clinical sites ( (b) (6) and (b) (6) ). Subject 450 (b) (6) enrolled in another bexagliflozin trial (C-480) while they were also enrolled in Trial C-450. It is unlikely that these violations significantly impact the results of the study.*
L1943: ## 15.1.5. Clinical Protocol Synopsis for C-476 (Version 8.0, Date: October 28, 2016)
L1944: **Sponsor:** TheracosBio, LLC.
L1945: **Name of Finished Product:** Bexagliflozin Tablets
L1946: **Name of Active Ingredient:** Bexagliflozin
L1947: **Study Title:** A Double-Blind Placebo-Controlled Study to Evaluate the Effects of Bexagliflozin on Hemoglobin A1c in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes and Increased Risk of Cardiovascular Adverse Events
L1948: **Study Number:** THR-1442-C-476
L1949: **Study Phase:** 3
L1950: **Primary Efficacy Objective:** The primary efficacy objective of this trial is to evaluate the placebo-adjusted change in HbA1c from baseline after 24 weeks of exposure to bexagliflozin in type 2 diabetic subjects at high risk of cardiovascular adverse events.
L1951: **Secondary Efficacy Objectives:**
L1952: The key secondary efficacy objectives are:
L1953: - To evaluate the effect of bexagliflozin compared to placebo on the change in HbA1c from baseline to Week 24 in randomized subjects who have been prescribed insulin to control their diabetes
- To evaluate the effect of bexagliflozin on the change in body weight from baseline to Week 48 in randomized subjects with a BMI \ge 25 kg/m^2 compared to placebo
- To evaluate the effect of bexagliflozin on the change in SBP from baseline to Week 24 in subjects with baseline systolic blood pressure \ge 140 mm Hg compared to placebo
L1954: Additional exploratory efficacy objectives are:
L1955: - To assess the effect of bexagliflozin treatment on the change in HbA1c versus placebo over time
- To evaluate the effect of bexagliflozin treatment on the change in FPG versus placebo over time
- To measure the proportion of subjects requiring an intensification of antidiabetic regimen versus placebo over time
- To measure the proportion of subjects requiring a relaxation of their antidiabetic regimen versus placebo over time
- To measure the incidence of hospitalization for heart failure among all subjects and among subjects with a history of heart failure at baseline.
L1956: **Safety Objectives:** The primary safety objective of this study is the contribution of at least 134 MACE+ to an eventual meta-analysis that is intended to exclude a hazard ratio of 1.8 or greater for subjects exposed to bexagliflozin compared to subjects exposed to placebo. MACE+ is defined as cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction (MI), nonfatal stroke, or hospitalization for unstable angina. An additional objective is the evaluation of the safety of exposure to bexagliflozin for a minimum of 52 weeks in a treatment population that is at elevated risk for major adverse cardiovascular events.
L1957: ## **Other Objectives:**
L1958: - Measurement of bexagliflozin plasma concentration as a function of time from dosing (sparsely sampled) will be conducted at 30 sites and will include approximately 240 subjects
- Measurement of cardiovascular biomarkers at baseline and Week 12 in an exploratory study to increase the understanding of bexagliflozin treatment effect on the biomarkers that are relevant in the CV disease diagnosis and prognosis
L1959: **Study Design:** C-476 is a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study. Approximately 1650 subjects with poorly controlled T2DM and at high risk of CV adverse events will be randomized to bexagliflozin tablets, 20 mg, or placebo in a ratio of 2:1 in addition to the background antidiabetic medications.
L1960: Potential participants with suboptimal glycemic control (HbA1c between 7.0% and 11%) despite treatment as recommended in local guidelines and at high risk of cardiovascular adverse events will enter a screening period of up to three weeks. Qualified participants will enter a single-blind, placebo run-in period to allow for diabetes education and optimization of compliance with diet and exercise recommendations. Qualified subjects will continue their prescreening regimen for glycemic control and will be instructed to take the run-in medication once daily for 13\pm2 days. Adjustment of treatment for hypertension or dyslipidemia will not be permitted during the screening and run-in periods although initiation of anticoagulant therapy (if clinically indicated) will be permitted. If a change in treatment is required to improve management of hypertension or dyslipidemia, the subject may re-enter the screening after the clinical condition and treatment regimen have not changed for at least four weeks. Subjects who continue to qualify for the study and who have demonstrated compliance by missing no more than one dose of the run-in doses as instructed will be randomized to receive the investigational product.
L1961: Assignment to treatment groups will be stratified by baseline HbA1c (&gt; or \le9.5%), baseline eGFR (eGFR \ge or &lt;60 mL/min/1.73 m2), baseline BMI (\ge or &lt;25 kg/m2), and history of heart failure. The study subjects will visit the clinic or complete phone interviews for evaluation at 2, 6, 12, 18, 24, 36, and 48 weeks postrandomization with subsequent visits scheduled every 24 weeks and a phone interview at 12 weeks after each clinic visit. The study duration will be determined by event accumulation. The treatment period will end when all randomized subjects have completed at least 52 weeks of treatment and a total of 134 subjects have experienced a MACE+. A follow-up visit will take place four weeks after the conclusion of treatment.
L1962: During the first 24 weeks of the efficacy assessment period, hyperglycemia should be managed with diet and exercise counseling. Changes in the medical therapy are allowed if the investigator feels it is necessary for the well-being of the subject. After 24 weeks, changes to the medical therapy for hyperglycemia should occur at the discretion of the investigator based on SMBG, FPG, and HbA1c information using local standards of care for subjects with T2DM. During the course of the study investigators will adjust other medications to affect changes in blood pressure and serum lipid values according to national or local guidelines. At every visit participants will be queried regarding adverse events and information on all events that potentially represent a MACE endpoint will be forwarded to a cardiovascular endpoint committee (CEC) for blinded adjudication. An investigator should also query the subject about symptoms that may be associated with possible DKA at every visit. A DKA adjudication committee will review and adjudicate all suspected DKA cases.
L1963: In this study, the incidence of MACE+ will be recorded for subsequent meta-analysis. MACE+ is defined as CV death, nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke, or hospitalization for unstable angina. It is estimated that the required total of 134 patients with a MACE+ will accrue over a treatment period of 2 to 3 years. During the trial, a DSMB will review the unblinded data periodically and may recommend an early termination of the trial for safety reasons. No interim analysis will be performed for efficacy assessment and the study will not be stopped for futility or benefit of bexagliflozin treatment.
L1964: Measurement of bexagliflozin plasma concentration as a function of time (sparsely sampled) will also be conducted at 30 centers and will include approximately 240 study subjects as part of a bexagliflozin population PK study. Samples will be drawn at Weeks 6 or 12. Cardiovascular biomarkers will be measured at baseline before treatment is administered and after 12 weeks of treatment in an exploratory study to evaluate the effect of bexagliflozin treatment on biomarkers that are relevant in cardiovascular disease diagnosis and prognosis.
L1965: **Study Population:** The study population will consist of approximately 1650 subjects who have been diagnosed with suboptimally controlled T2DM and who exhibit an elevated risk of cardiovascular events. The study population will comprise:
L1966: - Male or female adult subjects (age \ge 40 years)
- Subjects with a diagnosis of T2DM
- Subjects with HbA1c values of 7.0 to 11%, inclusive
- Subjects with FPG \le 300 mg/dL at screening
- Subjects who have a regimen for treatment of T2DM that has been stable for the past 3 months. A stable regimen is defined as: no changes in dose or frequency of oral hypoglycemic agents or GLP-1 agonists, or &lt;20% variability in total daily insulin dose.
- Subjects with either established cardiovascular disease or with multiple cardiovascular risk factors (if no documented cardiovascular disease) having the following attributes:**Group 1:** A history of atherosclerotic vascular disease as defined by one or more of the following: a) MI or ischemic (nonhemorrhagic) stroke &gt;3 months but \le 5 years prior to screening or b) documented history of coronary, carotid, or peripheral arterial revascularization (coronary artery bypass grafting must have occurred \ge 5 years prior to screening)
- **Group 2:** A history of New York Heart Association (NYHA) class II or class III heart failure (Appendix 4) at the time of screening. A history of heart failure is defined as:documented left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) \le 40\% and no subsequent LVEF &gt; 40\% within 6 months of screening, or
- an N-terminal probrain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) &gt; 300 pg/mL and no evidence of atrial fibrillation/flutter (AF) at the time of the screening ECG or an NT-proBNP &gt; 900 pg/mL and evidence of AF at the time of the screening ECG and (ii) either (a) structural heart disease documented by report of left atrial enlargement or left ventricular hypertrophy, or (b) exhibiting symptom(s) of HF requiring treatment with diuretic(s) for at least 30 days prior to screening
L1967: c. **Group 3:** Age \ge 55 years with 2 or more of the following:

- diabetes duration of \ge 10 years,
- uncontrolled hypertension defined as SBP &gt; 140 mm Hg despite 3 or more antihypertensive medications,
- current smoking,
- UACR &gt; 30 mg/g,
- eGFR of 45 to 60 mL/min/1.73 m^2, or
- high-density lipoprotein &lt; 1 mmol/L (38 mg/dL)
L1968: To ensure that subjects with various cardiovascular risks are adequately represented, a minimum of 352 subjects (21%) from each of the three groups will be recruited and \le 400 subjects who have a history of heart failure will be randomized in the study. The intended population is presented in Figure 46 below.

L1989: **Statistical Methods:** The primary endpoint is the difference in the change in HbA1c from Week 0 (randomization visit) to Week 24 among subjects exposed to bexagliflozin, 20 mg, compared to subjects exposed to placebo. Statistical significance will be declared at a two-sided 0.05 level of significance. The ITT population that includes all randomized subjects regardless of treatment adherence or availability of follow-up data will be analyzed. An MMRM ANCOVA with baseline HbA1c as a covariate will be performed on the available data, incorporating all visits from each patient at which HbA1c was measured.
L1990: Three key secondary endpoints are:
L1991: - Change in HbA1c from baseline to Week 24 in randomized subjects who have been prescribed insulin to control their diabetes
- Change in body weight from baseline to Week 48 in subjects with a BMI \ge 25 kg/m^2
- Change in SBP from baseline to Week 24 in subjects with baseline systolic blood pressure \ge 140 mm Hg
L1992: A hierarchical testing strategy in the following order will be undertaken, if the null hypothesis is excluded for the primary efficacy endpoint:
L1993: - Effect of bexagliflozin on the change in HbA1c from baseline to Week 24 in subjects who have been prescribed insulin to control diabetes at baseline, using MMRM ANCOVA adjusting for baseline HbA1c at a two-sided 0.05 level of significance; if a significant bexagliflozin effect is found, then:
- Comparison of treatments on the change in body weight at Week 48 in subjects with baseline BMI \ge 25 kg/m^2, using MMRM ANCOVA adjusting for baseline body weight, at a two-sided 0.05 level of significance; if a significant bexagliflozin effect is found, then:
- Comparison of treatments on the change in SBP at Week 24 in subjects with baseline systolic blood pressure \ge 140 mm Hg, using MMRM ANCOVA, adjusting for baseline SBP, at a two-sided 0.05 level of significance.
L1994: Additional effects of bexagliflozin on FPG, changes in HbA1c over time, changes in body weight over time, frequency of hospitalization for heart failure (in all subjects and in subjects with a history of heart failure), and general safety of bexagliflozin in subjects with T2DM will be analyzed as exploratory endpoint and will not be adjusted for multiplicity.
L1995: The sample size of 1650 patients is estimated based on the required number of events of MACE+ for the program-wide meta-analysis to assess bexagliflozin effect on cardiovascular safety and provides adequate power to compare treatments on the primary endpoint of change in HbA1c from baseline to 24 weeks.
L1996: Statistical analyses and summaries will be performed using SAS software (SAS Institute, Cary, NC).

L2013: ## 15.1.6. Clinical Protocol Synopsis for C-480 (Version 3.0, Date: October 27, 2016)
L2014: **Sponsor:** TheracosBio, LLC
L2015: **Name of Finished Product:** Bexagliflozin Tablets
L2016: **Name of Active Ingredient:** Bexagliflozin
L2017: **Study Title:** A Phase 3, Randomized, Double-Blind, Active-Controlled Study to Evaluate the Effects of Bexagliflozin versus Glimepiride in Subjects with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Who Have Inadequate Glycemic Control by Metformin
L2018: **Study Number:** THR-1442-C-480
L2019: **Study Phase:** 3
L2020: **Primary Objective:** The primary efficacy objective is to demonstrate that bexagliflozin is noninferior to glimepiride by evaluating the treatment effect on HbA1c reduction at Week 60 in subjects whose T2DM is inadequately controlled by metformin.
L2021: **Secondary Objectives:** The key secondary objectives are:
L2022: - To evaluate the treatment effect of bexagliflozin versus glimepiride on the change in body weight in subjects with baseline BMI \ge 25 kg/m^2 at Week 60
- To evaluate the treatment effect of bexagliflozin versus glimepiride on the change in SBP in subjects with baseline SBP \ge 140 mm Hg at Week 60
- To evaluate the treatment effect of bexagliflozin versus glimepiride on the difference in proportion of subjects with \ge 1 severe or documented symptomatic hypoglycemia events over 96 weeks
- To evaluate if bexagliflozin is superior to glimepiride on HbA1c reduction at Week 60
L2023: **Exploratory Objectives:**
L2024: - To assess the treatment effect of bexagliflozin versus glimepiride on the change in the proportion of subjects achieving HbA1c &lt;7.0% over time
L2025: - To assess the treatment effect of bexagliflozin versus glimepiride on the change in HbA1c over time
- To evaluate the treatment effect of bexagliflozin versus glimepiride on the change in FPG over time
- To assess the treatment effect of bexagliflozin versus glimepiride on the change in SBP over time
- To assess the treatment effect of bexagliflozin versus glimepiride on the change in body weight over time
- To assess the treatment effect of bexagliflozin versus glimepiride on the difference in proportion of subjects with \ge 1 severe or documented symptomatic hypoglycemia events over time
L2026: ## **Safety Objectives:**
L2027: - To compare the effects of bexagliflozin versus glimepiride on the incidence of adverse events of interest. Adverse events of interest are urinary tract infections including urosepsis and pyelonephritis, genital mycotic infections, diuretic effects including hypovolemia, hypotension episodes, hypoglycemia, hepatotoxicity, MACE, falls and fractures, malignancies, hypersensitivity reactions, acid-base disorders including diabetic ketoacidosis, and renal failure events.
- To compare the effects of bexagliflozin versus glimepiride on general safety assessments including treatment emergent adverse events, clinical laboratory events, 12-lead ECG parameters, physical examinations, vital signs including orthostatic blood pressure, and use of concomitant medications
L2028: ## **Other Objectives:**
L2029: - To compare the effects of bexagliflozin versus glimepiride on health-related quality of life using a validated instrument EQ-5D-3L.
L2030: **Study Design:** C-480 is a phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, parallel-group study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of bexagliflozin versus glimepiride in subjects with T2DM is inadequately controlled by metformin. A total of 420 subjects are planned to be randomized in a ratio of 1:1 to receive once daily treatment of active bexagliflozin with placebo glimepiride (Group 1) or placebo bexagliflozin with active glimepiride (Group 2) for 96 weeks in an outpatient setting. Active treatment in Group 1 will be bexagliflozin tablets, 20 mg. Active treatment in Group 2 will be glimepiride capsules, 2, 4, or 6 mg. At the time of screening, subjects will be taking metformin only (metformin-only) or metformin in addition to no more than one additional oral hypoglycemic agent (metformin-and-OHA). Study subjects will continue receiving open-labeled metformin background medication during the entire study.
L2031: The main eligibility criteria include 1) male or female subjects with T2DM and 2) screening HbA1c between 7.0% and 10.5% (inclusive) for subjects who are metformin-only treated, or screening HbA1c between 6.5% and 10.0% (inclusive) for subjects who are metformin-and-OHA treated. All eligible subjects must have taken metformin at a stable dose of \ge 1500 mg/day for at least 8 weeks prior to screening. Subjects who are metformin-and-OHA treated must be willing to undergo a 6-week wash-out of the non-metformin OHA prior to the start of a 2-week run-in period. During the wash-out, subjects will discontinue non-metformin OHA and continue taking metformin at the dose and frequency taken at screening.
L2032: All eligible subjects who are metformin-only treated or have completed the 6-week wash-out period will start a 2-week single-blind run-in period. During the run-in, subjects will receive placebo bexagliflozin and placebo glimepiride. Subjects who meet all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria prior to randomization will be eligible for randomization and receive investigational products.
L2033: During the treatment period, glimepiride will be provided in three dose levels: 2 mg, 4 mg, and 6 mg. Placebo glimepiride will also be provided in three dose levels: placebo for 2 mg, placebo for 4 mg, and placebo for 6 mg. Subjects will receive the starting dose of glimepiride, 2 mg or placebo. Subjects who meet protocol-specified glycemic criteria will undergo up-titration of the glimepiride dose at Weeks 2, 4, and 6. The dose will be increased to the next dosing level if during the preceding 2 weeks: (1) \ge 50\% of fasting SMBG measurements &gt;110 mg/dL and (2) no severe or documented symptomatic hypoglycemia events. Subjects assigned to receive placebo glimepiride, will receive mock titrations of glimepiride at Weeks 2, 4, and 6 based on the same glycemic criteria. No dose changes of glimepiride will occur after 6 weeks of treatment.
L2034: Each subject will be instructed to return to the clinic at Weeks 0, 2, 4, 6, 12, 24, 36, 48, 60, 72, 84 (off-site phone visit), and 96 for efficacy assessment and safety monitoring. Subjects will return to the clinic for a follow-up exit visit at Week 98 or 2 weeks after last dose of study drug if subjects early terminate prior to Week 96.
L2035: During the study, a DSMB will review the unblinded data periodically and may recommend early termination of the trial for safety reasons. In the event of administrative changes or other related reasons, the Sponsor reserves the rights to terminate the study early. There will be no interim analysis; final statistical analysis will be performed after all subjects complete the study.
L2036: **Study Population and Main Eligibility Criteria:** A total of 420 eligible subjects are planned for this study. The study population will comprise:
L2037: - Male or female adult subjects \ge 18 years of age
- If subjects are female of childbearing potential, subjects must be negative on the urine pregnancy test and agree to abstain from coitus or use contraception during the entire study to avoid any possible pregnancy
- Subjects who are in one of the two categories:Metformin-only treated: receive \ge 1500 mg/day metformin only for at least 8 weeks prior to screening or
- Metformin-and-OHA treated: receive \ge 1500 mg/day metformin for at least 8 weeks prior to screening and \ge 14 days of 1 additional OHA in the 8 weeks prior to screening.
- Subjects with a diagnosis of T2DM with HbA1c levels between 7.0% and 10.5% (inclusive) at screening if metformin-only treated or with HbA1c levels between 6.5% and 10.0% (inclusive) at screening if metformin- and-OHA treated
- Subjects with a BMI \le 45 kg/m^2 at screening
- If applicable, taking stable doses of treatment for dyslipidemia and/or hypertension for 30 days prior to screening. Subjects do not need to be treated for dyslipidemia or hypertension to be eligible for the study
- Subjects who are willing and able to return for all clinic visits and to complete all study-required procedures, including SMBG measurements
L2038: Prior to randomization, all subjects must:
L2039: - Maintain adequate glycemic control during the washout and run-in periods (fasting plasma glucose values are not \ge 250 mg/dL on consecutive days)
- Have an HbA1c between 7.0% and 10.5% (inclusive) at Visit V5
- Adhere to the investigational product administration requirements as evidenced by missing no more than two placebo run-in medication doses of any kind

L2041: Once daily oral administration of bexagliflozin and glimepiride
L2042: - Group 1: bexagliflozin tablets, 20 mg, and glimepiride capsules, placebo
- Group 2: bexagliflozin tablets, placebo, and glimepiride capsules, 2 mg, 4 mg, or 6 mg
L2043: **Duration of Treatment:** Eligible subjects will receive a total treatment duration of 98 weeks including 2 weeks of run-in medications and 96 weeks of investigational products.

L2046: - Change in HbA1c from baseline at Week 60
