L2908: ## 17.1.8. Summary and Conclusions
L2909: ## 17.1.8.1. Statistical Issues
L2910: There were no significant statistical concerns identified in this review on the design, conduct, and analyses of the primary and secondary CV endpoints.
L2911: ## 17.1.8.2. Collective Evidence
L2912: In the NDA submission, data from nine randomized controlled phase 2/3 trials were synthesized to evaluate the cardiovascular risk associated with the use of bexagliflozin, according to a prespecified CV meta-analysis plan. Eight of the nine trials are efficacy trials with fixed treatment period, while Trial C-476 is a dedicated event-driven cardiovascular outcomes trial with a primary objective to collect CV events to be combined with other efficacy trials in the CV meta-analysis.
L2913: A total of 4090 subjects were included in the FAS for the CV meta-analysis, with 2437 in the bexagliflozin arm and 1653 in the combined control arm. Among them, a total of 1699 subjects were randomized in Trial C-476, which enrolled a population with elevated CV risk and contributed about 69% of the total follow-up time in the CV meta-analysis.
L2914: The prespecified primary composite endpoint for CV safety evaluation was MACE+, comprised of CV death (including deaths of unknown cause), nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, and hospitalization for unstable angina. Among the 4090 FAS subjects, a total of 159 subjects experienced at least one adjudicated MACE+ event during the course of the trials, with 96 subjects in the pooled bexagliflozin group and 63 subjects in the pooled control group. Most of these events (89 in the bexagliflozin arm and 57 in the placebo arm) were observed in Trial C-476. The primary analysis was a time-to-event analysis based on a stratified Cox proportional hazards model with the meta-analysis study group (C-476 or not) as the stratification factor. The primary analysis resulted in a hazard ratio estimate of 0.80 with an associated 95% confidence interval of (0.58, 1.09). The upper bound of 1.09 was lower than the 1.8 risk margin preset for the nonexcess risk hypothesis on this endpoint, and it can be concluded that the analysis for MACE+ successfully ruled out the 1.8 risk margin. Analyses with on-treatment censoring schemes, analysis of an expanded 6-component MACE endpoint and each of its component events support the conclusion for MACE+. Analyses of MACE+ across a range of subgroups were generally consistent and showed no evidence of increased risk associated with bexagliflozin.
L2915: According to a prespecified hierarchical testing procedure, the first key secondary endpoint 3-component MACE (CV death including deaths of unknown cause, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke) was then evaluated for nonexcess risk against a preset margin of 1.3. Prespecified time-to-event analysis using a similar Cox model as that used for MACE+, resulted in a hazard ratio estimate of 0.82 with a 95% confidence interval (0.59, 1.13). Therefore, the analysis for strict MACE successfully ruled out the 1.3 risk margin.
L2916: The second key secondary endpoint, which was the composite of CV death and hospitalization for heart failure was tested for superiority as the next step of the testing hierarchy. The null
L2917: hypothesis was not rejected; therefore, the objective of demonstrating superiority was not achieved for this endpoint.
L2918: In this CV meta-analysis, the overall results were highly influenced by the single CV outcomes Trial C-476 due to its population of high CV risk, large sample size and long follow up for CV events. Only 13 adjudicated MACE+ events out of the 159 primary CV events were contributed by other phase 2/3 trials. This is expected and preplanned. Analysis results of the primary and secondary endpoints were also examined for Trial C-476 alone and they are consistent with the overall results of the meta-analysis.
L2919: ## 17.1.8.3. Conclusions and Recommendations
L2920: Theracos evaluated the cardiovascular safety of bexagliflozin through a prespecified CV meta-analysis of its phase 2/3 programs. The prespecified stratified Cox proportional hazards model obtained an estimated hazard ratio for the primary cardiovascular endpoint MACE+ (4-component: cardiovascular death including deaths of unknown cause, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or hospitalization for unstable angina) of 0.80 with an associated 95% confidence interval of (0.58, 1.09). The upper bound of this confidence interval was smaller than 1.8 and therefore met the preset risk margin for MACE+. The stratified Cox proportional hazards model obtained an estimated hazard ratio for the key secondary endpoint MACE (3-component: cardiovascular death including deaths of unknown cause, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke) of 0.82 with a 95% confidence interval of (0.59, 1.13). The upper bound was smaller than 1.3 and therefore met the preset risk margin for strict MACE.
L2921: In conclusion, based on our statistical review on results of the prespecified CV meta-analysis, bexagliflozin is not associated with an unacceptable increase in cardiovascular risk.
L2922: ## 17.2. Applicant's Approach to the Safety Review
L2923: The Applicant performed their integrated safety analysis primarily utilizing a pool that consisted of all phase 2b/3 trials conducted in the clinical development program for bexagliflozin for improved glycemic control enrolling subjects with diabetes, as well as a subset of diabetic subjects enrolled in trials conducted in the clinical program of bexagliflozin for the treatment of essential hypertension (C-603A and C-603B), termed the “overall diabetic pool.” C-603A was randomized, controlled trial where hypertensive subjects were randomized 1:1 to receive bexagliflozin 20 mg or placebo for 12 weeks. Subjects who completed C-603A immediately initiated C-603B, which was a randomized withdrawal trial. For both trials, AEs that occurred while subjects were randomized to placebo were not defined as treatment emergent in the Applicant’s analysis. To address this, a modified pool was created, termed the “broad pool,” which included all studies in the Applicant’s overall diabetic pool; however, only data from the placebo-controlled portion of C-603A (including both diabetic and nondiabetic subjects) was included. As the broad pool combines trials of different study design, patient population, and drug formulation (i.e., C-418), this pool was used for exploratory purposes in this safety review.
L2924: In addition, the Applicant also utilized a pool consisting of placebo-controlled trials where bexagliflozin was evaluated as monotherapy or as add-on to metformin, termed the “general diabetic population,” which consisted to C-418, C-419, C-449, and C-450. However, as C-418 used a noncommercial formulation of bexagliflozin and had differing trial design features as
L2925: compared to the other trials (e.g., longer duration, lack of a washout period for subjects taking one oral antihyperglycemic agent prior to randomization, etc.), the review team concluded it was not appropriate for labeling purposes. A modified pool, consisting of C-419, C-449, and C-450, termed the placebo-controlled pool, was used in FDA's review to inform product labeling.
L2926: Lastly, to identify adverse events associated with bexagliflozin treatment in the integrated summary of safety (ISS), the Applicant utilized statistical strategies (e.g., Fisher's exact test). The review team did not agree with the Applicant's use of statistical methods for identifying safety signals and this approach was not utilized in the FDA's safety review.
L2927: Overall, the FDA's safety review utilized modified data pools as compared to the pools utilized by the Applicant and did not rely on statistical testing to identify safety signals. The impact of these differences in the approach to the safety review is reflected in the modifications made to the proposed labeling (see Section 21 for a summary of labeling negotiations).
L2928: ## 17.3. Submission-Specific Safety Issues
L2929: The following sections detail submission-specific safety issues, including the following AESIs: DKA, diuretic effects, fractures, falls, GMI, hepatotoxicity, rash, hypoglycemia, hypotensive episodes, malignancies, acute kidney injury (AKI), pyelonephritis/urosepsis, and hypersensitivity reactions. Hypoglycemia, with and without concurrent use with insulin or an insulin secretagogue, is also discussed. C-476 was the largest and longest trial in the bexagliflozin clinical development program, enrolling subjects who were older and with a longer diabetes duration and more comorbidities as compared to other trials. Therefore, Trial C-476 was considered the most relevant trial to inform events that may occur at a low frequency, events that may be more likely to occur with prolonged drug exposure, and/or events that may have a latency period. Additional trial data are reviewed where relevant.
L2930: ## 17.3.1. Fracture
L2931: Conflicting evidence exists with regards to whether SGLT2 inhibitor treatment may increase the risk of fracture events. Bone safety was initially an area of possible concern for this drug class due to the potential for altered renal tubule reabsorption of calcium and phosphorus, the potential for altered vitamin D metabolism, the tendency for weight loss, and preclinical bone findings of hyperostosis in rats. In the approval letter for canagliflozin, a postmarketing requirement (PMR) was issued to assess the impact of canagliflozin on bone mineral density (BMD) and markers of bone turnover (PMR 2027-4). To address the PMR, the Applicant was required to complete trial DIA3010. This trial, which was intended to evaluate glycemic efficacy in older adults, was a placebo-controlled, double-blind trial randomizing subjects who were \ge 55 to \le 80 years of age to placebo, canagliflozin 100 mg, or canagliflozin 300 mg (Bilezikian et al. 2016). The primary efficacy endpoint was change in HbA1c from baseline to Week 26, with a placebo-controlled extension period for the assessment of secondary safety endpoints, including those related to bone safety. BMD was measured by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry in 714 older adults (mean age 64 years). At 2 years, subjects randomized to canagliflozin 100 mg and 300 mg had placebo-corrected declines in BMD at the total hip of 0.9% and 1.2%, respectively, and at the lumbar spine of 0.3% and 0.7%, respectively. Of the CVOTs conducted for this drug class, including CANVAS and CANVAS-R for canagliflozin, EMPA-REG for empagliflozin, DECLARE for
L2932: dapagliflozin, and VERTIS for ertugliflozin, an increased risk of fracture was only observed in the CANVAS trial (HR: 1.55; 95% CI: 1.21, 1.97). However, no increased risk was observed in the CANVAS-R trial (HR: 0.86; 95% CI: 0.62, 1.19), despite the enrollment of similar subject populations. Currently, the US prescribing information for canagliflozin includes a Warnings and Precautions statement for risk of bone fracture risk. While other SGLT2 inhibitor labeling does not include a similar Warnings and Precautions statement, the dapagliflozin US prescribing information reports that in a placebo-controlled study of subjects with an eGFR \ge 30 to &lt;60 mL/min/1.73 m^2 with a 2:1 randomization allocation, 13 subjects receiving dapagliflozin experienced bone fractures compared to none receiving placebo over a 104-week treatment period. Investigation of this imbalance revealed that all fractures were related to falls and that 7/13 subjects had a history of orthostatic hypotension or diabetic neuropathy. Although small, inconsistent changes in bone biomarkers were observed, including parathyroid hormone concentration, calcium, 25-OH vitamin D, phosphorus and magnesium, the imbalance was not reproduced when all subjects with moderate renal dysfunction in the phase 2b and phase 3 trials were pooled. A consult from the Division of Bone, Reproductive and Urologic Products concluded that there was insufficient evidence that dapagliflozin was associated with bone loss or increased fracture risk.
L2933: As identified by Food and Drug Administration Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities query (FMQ), there was no imbalance in the overall frequency of fracture events in C-476 (4.0% and 3.9% of subjects reporting at least one fracture event in the bexagliflozin and placebo groups, respectively, as identified by the “Fracture” FMQ). However, more subjects in the bexagliflozin group (15 subjects (1.3%)) experienced a serious fracture event as compared to the placebo group (2 subjects (0.4%)), including serious events of hip and femur fracture (Table 207). The narratives for serious fracture events were reviewed, which did not reveal any overt trends that indicated drug relatedness (e.g., falls and fractures due secondary to hypotensive episodes) (Table 208). The majority of fracture events occurred in C-476, and other trials did not accrue enough events to meaningfully inform this signal.
L2934: As discussed in Section 17.3.2, there was no imbalance of fall events in C-476, although undercoding of fall events in the ADaM adverse events analysis (ADAE) dataset limits interpretability of these findings (see Section 7.7.3). There was a lower incidence of osteoporosis events in the bexagliflozin group in C-476 as identified by the “Osteoporosis” FMQ, although data were limited (3 (0.3%) versus 5 (0.9%) subjects experiencing an event in the bexagliflozin and placebo groups, respectively). The majority of serious fracture events in C-476 occurred in subjects older than 65 years with baseline eGFR &gt;60 mL/min/1.73 m^2; however, the low number of events in each subgroup limits meaningful conclusions. There was no imbalance in fracture events in the dedicated renal impairment trial in the bexagliflozin clinical program, although data were limited (1.9% of subjects with a fracture event in each treatment group).

L2949: While fracture events were prespecified AESIs in the bexagliflozin clinical program, monitoring for these events beyond passive reporting did not occur. For example, the Applicant did not employ a specific data collection form, any prespecified follow-up investigations in the study protocol, or independent review. While standard chemistry laboratory parameters were collected, more specific markers for bone turnover (e.g., parathyroid hormone, collagen type 1 beta-carboxy telopeptide) were not evaluated, nor was an assessment of BMD carried out. Lack of additional information complicates the assessment of the noted imbalance in serious fracture events observed in C-476. Only one event indicative of increased parathyroid hormone was observed in C-476; an event of “Hyperparathyroidism secondary” that occurred in the bexagliflozin group. Regarding the available laboratory data, there were no clinically meaningful differences between bexagliflozin and placebo in terms of changes in serum calcium or alkaline phosphatase; however, bexagliflozin treatment mildly increases serum magnesium and phosphate (see Section 17.4 for additional information on laboratory analyses). The meaningfulness of these laboratory changes on long-term bone safety is uncertain.
L2950: ***FDA Reviewer Comment:*** *Case narratives for the serious fracture events identified a substantial number of causes that were associated with high-impact trauma (e.g., snowmobile accident, hit by crane hook, motorcycle accident, fall from excavator, direct trauma from heavy object) that appear unrelated to the drug. Restricting the data to nontraumatic serious fractures significantly diminishes the imbalance. However, when evaluating osteoporosis trials, fractures of the vertebrae, hip, forearm and humerus (other than pathologic) are generally considered potentially relevant to bony integrity regardless of trauma severity, and fractures of the hand, foot, skull or face are typically disregarded (see dapagliflozin DBRUP consult for further information). Furthermore, despite the lack of data on parathyroid hormone levels and bone mineral density, the laboratory biomarkers related to bone health that were collected (calcium, magnesium, phosphorus, alkaline phosphatase) were not consistent with decreased substrate concentrations for bone mineralization or suggested increased bone fragility. Despite unclear drug-relatedness, labeling in Section 6 to inform providers of the potential risk of increased fracture with bexagliflozin treatment is proposed given that fracture events were serious in nature, including events of serious hip and femur fracture.*
L2951: ## 17.3.2. Falls
L2952: Similar to fracture events, conflicting evidence exists with regards to whether SGLT2 inhibitor treatment may increase the risk of falls, with only canagliflozin currently labeled for increased risk of fall events. Specifically, in a pool of nine clinical trials with mean duration of exposure to canagliflozin of 85 weeks, the proportion of subjects who experienced falls was 1.3%, 1.5%, and 2.1% with comparator, canagliflozin 100 mg, and canagliflozin 300 mg, respectively. The higher risk of falls for subjects treated with canagliflozin was observed within the first few weeks of treatment.
L2953: As detailed in Section 7.7.3, fall events were found in narrative descriptions of SAEs that were not included in the ADAE dataset originally submitted to this application, and an updated ADAE dataset utilizing natural language processing (NLP) found a significant number of additional events. The reason fall events were not adequately captured in the original ADAE dataset appears multifactorial, including lack of specific protocol-driven procedures to collect fall events, fall events potentially being incorrectly assessed as a symptom of an event as opposed to
L2954: a stand-alone event or sequelae of a separate event, and inappropriate Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) coding (i.e., “left ankle pain due to fall” coded as “pain ankle” without coding of “fall”). Despite these issues, no imbalance in fall events was observed in the ADAE dataset submitted with the application or with the NLP-modified dataset (Table 209). As discussed in Section 7.7.3, there is no evidence of systemic bias with regards to missed events, including fall events, in the ADAE dataset. Bexagliflozin does not appear to be associated with increased risk of fall events based on the available data. In addition, the imbalance in fracture events is proposed for the labeling in Section 6, despite the limitations of the study/dataset.

L2959: ## 17.3.3. Malignancy
L2960: At the time the bexagliflozin clinical program was initiated, it was unknown whether SGLT2 inhibitor treatment was associated with malignancy. Given this, malignancy events were considered AESIs. Premarket and postmarket data from other approved drugs in the class generally appears to support that SGLT2 inhibitor treatment does not increase malignancy risk; however, canagliflozin includes labeling to inform providers on imbalances observed in renal cell carcinoma events that occurred in the CANVAS trial.
L2961: Given that malignancies typically have a long latency period, C-476 was determined to be the most relevant trial for the assessment of malignancy. As identified by the FMQ for “Malignancy,” there were 39 (3.4%) and 18 (3.2%) subjects having at least one malignancy event in the bexagliflozin and placebo groups, respectively (Table 210). As shown in Table 210, most events occurred in two or fewer subjects, limiting interpretability. As discussed below, several categories of malignancies (i.e., lung cancers, skin cancers) demonstrated imbalances unfavorable to drug when preferred terms (PTs) of similar medical concept were grouped.
L2962: An imbalance in nonmelanoma skin cancers was apparent in C-476, with more subjects having an event of “squamous cell carcinoma,” “basal cell carcinoma,” “squamous cell carcinoma of skin,” and “skin cancer” in the bexagliflozin group (17 (1.5%) subjects with an event) as compared to the placebo group (3 (0.5%) subjects with an event). A time-to-event analysis showed events mostly occurred within the first 18 months of treatment in the bexagliflozin group (Figure 71). Importantly, the time-to-event analysis also highlights that multiple lesions were also reported for some subjects, and that there were 11 (0.97%) versus 3 (0.57%) subjects who had a nonmelanoma event in C-476 therefore lessening the imbalance between groups, particularly when accounting for the 2:1 randomization.
L2963: Risk factors for squamous cell and basal cell carcinoma include fair skin, older age, male gender, UV exposure, and history of skin cancer. Demographics for these subjects were reviewed, and subjects were generally Caucasian, over 65 years of age, and male. The anatomical location of the lesion was generally in a location where sun exposure would be expected (e.g., face, neck,
L2964: arm, etc.). In nonclinical studies, bexagliflozin did not absorb UV light between 290 to 700 nm, and therefore nonclinical studies to investigate potential photosensitivity effects were not conducted. Events in the “Photosensitivity and photodermatosis conditions” HLT were reviewed; however, only three events occurred in C-476, limiting interpretability. Carcinogenicity studies were conducted in rats and mice, with no treatment-related tumor findings in either species. A meta-analysis that utilized a systematic search of electronic databases did not show an increased risk of melanoma and nonmelanoma skin cancers with SGLT2 inhibitor use (Tang et al. 2018). While canagliflozin is labeled for photosensitivity events, nonclinical studies demonstrated UV absorption of the compound, prompting additional characterization of potential photosensitivity reactions. Overall, the clinical meaningfulness of this signal is unclear; however, there were no events resulting in death, they were not judged as serious by the investigator, and did not result in treatment discontinuation.
L2965: In C-476, there was a minor unfavorable imbalance in events of lung cancer (PTs of “Lung adenocarcinoma,” “Squamous cell carcinoma of lung,” “Lung neoplasm malignant,” and “Nonsmall cell lung cancer”; 5 (0.4%) versus 1 (0.2%) events in the bexagliflozin and placebo groups, respectively). All subjects had a history of heavy smoking, ranging from 28 to 60 pack-years, except for one subject where smoking history was not reported. Conclusions are limited when considering the 2:1 randomization and low event rate.
L2966: In the Applicant’s analysis of the overall diabetic pool, they note a minor imbalance in events of non-Hodgkin’s Lymphoma, with four events occurring in bexagliflozin exposed subjects (0.10 cases per 100 subject-years of exposure) as compared to none in placebo- or active-comparator-exposed subjects. Based on the available data, causality cannot be assessed.
L2967: With regard to malignancy signals from other SGLT2 inhibitor programs, pheochromocytoma, Leydig cell tumor, and renal cell carcinoma were concerns with canagliflozin treatment upon approval. Currently, the US prescribing information for canagliflozin described an imbalance unfavorable to drug in renal cell carcinoma events in the CANVAS trial, although the label states that a causal relationship could not be established due to the limited number of cases. There was no imbalance in renal cell carcinoma events in C-476 (2 (0.2%) versus 1 (0.2%) subjects with an event in the bexagliflozin and placebo groups, respectively), although few events limits interpretability. No events of Leydig cell tumor or pheochromocytoma were observed in the bexagliflozin clinical program.
L2968: Bladder cancer was initially a concern with dapagliflozin treatment and a PMR was issued to assess the risk of bladder cancer associated with dapagliflozin in the DECLARE trial (PMR 2121-6). As discussed in the clinical review for the DECLARE trial, this trial excluded an unacceptable increased risk of bladder cancer in the studied population and the US prescribing information was updated accordingly (see Dr. Carey’s review in DARRTS dated October 15, 2019). Three events of transitional cell carcinoma were observed in C-476, which upon narrative review appear to also have involved the bladder. Limited data impedes interpretability of this finding.
L2969: Overall, the available data do not support increased risk of malignancy with bexagliflozin treatment, although it is acknowledged that data was limited. As stated above, there is no known causal relationship with SGLT2 inhibitor treatment and malignancy.

L2976: ## 17.3.4. Hypersensitivity and Rash
L2977: (b) (4) The Applicant describes that rash was a concern early in the bexagliflozin development program because one subject in the multiple ascending dose segment of the phase 1 Trial C-328 developed a rash and withdrew, and another subject of the phase 2b Trial C-418 developed a moderate severity event of rash that was likely due to bexagliflozin exposure based on a withdrawal and rechallenge test. In addition, a scientist working on formulation development developed a rash that was addressed by use of personal protective garments. All events occurred with exposure to the noncommercial, capsule formulation of bexagliflozin. In response to this safety signal, the Applicant reformulated the drug to the proposed, to-be-commercialized tablet formulation that employs a gastroretentive mechanism. Following the introduction of the tablet formulation, the Applicant reports one moderate event of allergic dermatitis that resolved with interruption of dosing and recurred upon resumption of dosing in Trial C-603A. The Applicant states that events of rash/dermatitis should be considered confirmed adverse reactions associated with exposure to bexagliflozin based on these findings.
L2978: FMQs for “Rash,” “Urticaria,” “Erythema,” “Angioedema,” “Hypersensitivity,” and “Anaphylactic reaction” were utilized to investigate rash and hypersensitivity events. In C-476, 5.4% and 3.4% of subjects in the bexagliflozin and placebo groups experienced at least one event of rash, respectively, as determined by the Rash FMQ (Table 211). Some events of genital rash were captured in this query, which may be more likely related to cases of GMI as compared to
L2979: generalized rash events; however, exclusion of this preferred term from the analysis did not significantly impact the results (data not shown). Events of rash were generally evaluated as mild to moderate intensity by the investigator, with only one event being evaluated as serious. The narrative for this SAE was reviewed. Subject 476-(b) (6), assigned to the bexagliflozin group, experienced events of “dermatitis allergic” and “dermatitis contact” after the initiation of afatinib for the treatment of metastatic lung adenocarcinoma. Cutaneous reactions are known adverse reactions associated with afatinib treatment as described in the US prescribing information, and therefore this event may not be related to bexagliflozin exposure. More events of rash led to treatment discontinuation in the placebo group as compared to the bexagliflozin group of C-476 (1 event (&lt;0.1%) versus 3 events (0.5%) in the bexagliflozin and placebo groups, respectively). A time-to-event analysis showed that rash events appear to occur at a somewhat constant rate over time (Figure 72). While data from other trials was limited, an imbalance unfavorable to drug for events of rash as identified by FMQ was also observed in the placebo-controlled pool (1.3% versus 0% in the bexagliflozin and placebo groups, respectively). No rash events in the placebo-controlled pool were serious or led to discontinuation from the trial.
L2980: A higher incidence of hypersensitivity events was observed in the bexagliflozin group (1.3%) as compared to the placebo group (0.7%) in C-476. No events were serious or led to discontinuation. Few events were captured in the FMQs for “Erythema,” “Urticaria,” and “Anaphylactic reaction” limiting interpretability (Table 211).

L2987: ***FDA Reviewer Comment:*** Overall, an increased incidence of rash was observed in C-476 and the placebo-controlled pool. This observation in combination with the Applicant's description of the rechallenge events may support drug relatedness. However, rash events were generally not serious, nor did they typically lead to discontinuation. Skin reactions including rash and urticaria have been identified in postmarketing reports for dapagliflozin and empagliflozin, and these events are reported in the current US prescribing information for these products. Several literature reports also seem to support the possibility of increased skin reactions associated with SGLT2 inhibitor exposure (Damiani et al. 2016; Raschi et al. 2017; Sakaeda et al. 2018). It is appropriate that information regarding rash be described in Section 6 of the labeling for bexagliflozin. A Warnings and Precautions statement is not necessary to describe the rash events observed, which, as noted above, were generally not serious nor did they typically lead to discontinuation.
L2988: While no serious hypersensitivity or anaphylactic reactions were characterized, the frequency of these events may be too low to evaluate in a premarket setting. Hypersensitivity to the drug and any excipients is included as a contraindication in labeling for SGLT2 inhibitors, which also appears appropriate for bexagliflozin.
L2989: ## 17.3.5. Hepatic Injury
L2990: Hepatic injury events were evaluated as AESIs in the bexagliflozin clinical program to assess the relationship between bexagliflozin and drug-induced liver injury (DILI). For any increase in alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and/or aspartate aminotransferase (AST) &gt;3x upper limit of
L2991: normal (ULN), investigators were instructed to confirm the hepatic enzyme elevation within 48 to 72 hours and to assess the clinical situation at least every 96 hours until ALT and/or AST return to &lt;2.5 \times ULN. Investigators were advised to stop study medication and report the event as an AE if the enzyme elevation was confirmed or worsening. Hepatotoxicity was entered as an AE should any of the following have occurred:
L2992: - ALT or AST &gt;8 \times ULN
- ALT or AST &gt;3 \times ULN and total bilirubin &gt;2 \times ULN or international normalized ratio (INR) &gt;1.5
- ALT or AST &gt;3 \times ULN with the appearance of fatigue, nausea, vomiting, right upper quadrant pain or tenderness, fever, rash, and/or eosinophilia (&gt;5\%)
L2993: Investigators were instructed to permanently discontinue the study medication should a hepatotoxicity event occur. Note, the Applicant's hepatotoxicity definition did not consider elevations in ALP that could be indicative of cholestasis, and ALP was not systematically assessed in all trials. For trials where ALP data were not available (i.e., C-448 and C-450), Hy's law analysis was completed irrespective of ALP information for the assessment of DILI.
L2994: The broad pool, which pools all data from phase 2b/3 trials utilizing the 20 mg dosage strength (see Section 17.2 for additional information), was used to identify potential Hy's Law cases (Figure 73 and Table 212). No Hy's Law cases were identified from available lab data. Enzyme elevations in the cholestasis and Temple's Corollary quadrants were generally balanced between bexagliflozin and placebo groups (Table 212). There were 0.64 versus 1.08 subjects per 100 patient-years in the pooled bexagliflozin and placebo groups of the broad pool, respectively, that experienced at least one hepatic injury event as assessed by FMQ. While there were no overall concerning trends indicating DILI, selected narratives of subjects with outlier values were reviewed. Narratives reviewed indicated potentially alternative etiologies and were inconclusive with regards to drug relatedness. For example, Subject 476-[REDACTED](b)(6) was a 53-year-old Asian male assigned to the bexagliflozin group who had a history of hepatic steatosis, dyslipidemia, cholelithiasis, and hepatitis B infection. The subject experienced a solitary elevation of ALT and AST to 16.8 \times and 14.7 \times ULN, respectively, with an increase in total bilirubin to 1.29 \times ULN (this subject represents the most extreme LFT observed in the clinical program as observed as the rightmost point in Temple's Corollary quadrant in Figure 73). In addition to chronic active hepatitis B, the subject experienced recurrent infectious cholecystitis during the trial, indicating a potential alternative etiology for the LFT elevations observed. Lastly, as discussed in Section 17.4, there were no noteworthy mean changes in bilirubin over time, and modest decreases in mean ALT and AST in the placebo-controlled pool, and subjects with one or more liver chemistry analyte values exceeding specified levels was also generally balanced between treatment arms in the placebo-controlled pool, Trial C-476, and Trial C-448. Overall, there does not appear to be a signal for DILI based on the information available.

L3000: ## 17.3.6. DKA
L3001: DKA is a serious, acute complication of diabetes that may be potentially life-threatening. The association between SGLT2 inhibitor treatment and increased risk of DKA was identified from postmarketing reports for approved products while the clinical development program for bexagliflozin was ongoing. A “DKA Monitoring and Adjudication Plan” was initiated January 2016 to enable relevant data to be captured and consistently adjudicated in the bexagliflozin clinical program. Trials C-450, C-448, C-480, and C-476 were ongoing at the time the monitoring plan was initiated. For these trials, protocols were updated via protocol amendments to include DKA as an AESI, to describe the DKA monitoring procedures to investigators, and to add a dedicated DKA case report form (CRF). These monitoring and documentation procedures were incorporated into protocols for all trials initiated after January 2016 (i.e., C-419, C-423, C-603). Trials C-418 and C-449 were completed prior to initiation of the DKA Monitoring and
L3002: Adjudication Plan, and data from adverse event logs, SAE reports, and laboratory parameters were used to identify potential DKA events retrospectively.
L3003: As detailed in the DKA Monitoring and Adjudication Plan, suspected DKA cases could be identified based on subject-reported events, investigator-reported events, or adjudicator-identified events. Subjects were informed of the signs and symptoms of DKA and were instructed to call the study site and seek treatment should such signs or symptoms occur, although ketone monitoring via home-use meter was not carried out in any trial. Investigators were informed that DKA may occur in the absence of highly elevated plasma glucose (i.e., euglycemic DKA). DKA CRFs were to be completed by the investigators at all subject visits (i.e., scheduled visits, unscheduled visits, phone consultations, etc.). The eCRFs were designed to document whether a suspected DKA had occurred and to ensure the collection of relevant clinical information to allow for adjudication. All potential DKA events underwent blinded adjudication by an endocrinologist. In addition, a listing of SAEs was sent to the adjudicator to identify DKA events potentially missed by investigators.
L3004: As shown in Table 213, DKA was categorized by the adjudicator as either confirmed DKA, probable DKA, possible DKA, unlikely DKA, or intermediate DKA. The Applicant's DKA monitoring plan, including DKA case definitions, were discussed with the agency and agreed to during IND interactions (see Written Response Only dated September 21, 2016 in DARRTS).
L3005: **Table 213. DKA Case Definitions**
L3006: Case Term	Case Definition
Confirmed DKA	An episode consisting of symptoms of DKA with ketonuria or ketonemia AND one or more biochemical findings of acidosis, which responds to fluid replenishment and, if needed, insulin
Probable DKA	An episode consisting of moderate/severe symptoms of DKA, which responds to fluid replenishment and, if needed, insulin; OR
An episode consisting of moderate/severe symptoms of DKA with moderate to large ketonuria and/or ketonemia without biochemical findings of acidosis, which responds to fluid replenishment and, if needed, insulin
Possible DKA	An episode consisting of mild to moderate symptoms of DKA with small to moderate ketonuria, condition self-managed, and resolves with or without change in diabetic medications; OR
An episode of 4+ (40 mg/dL) or greater ketonuria with mild symptoms of DKA; OR
An episode of 5+ (80 mg/dL) or greater ketonuria without symptoms of DKA
Unlikely DKA	An episode consisting of mild symptoms of DKA with negative to small ketonuria; OR
Small to moderate (2+) ketonuria without symptoms
Indeterminant DKA	Mild to moderate symptoms of DKA without ketosis that are self-managed and/or self-resolving

L3008: Abbreviations: DKA diabetic ketoacidosis.
L3009: The following definitions were specified in the DKA Monitoring and Adjudication Plan:
L3010: - One or more biochemical findings of acidosis shall mean one or more of: (i) a venous pH &lt;7.3 or an arterial pH ≤7.3; (ii) a plasma bicarbonate &lt;18 mM; or (iii) an albumin-corrected anion gap &gt;10 mM.
L3011: - Symptoms of DKA shall mean exhibiting: (i) nausea with or without vomiting; (ii) abdominal pain; (iii) tachypnea and/or hyperpnea; (v) polydipsia; (vi) polyuria; (vii) malaise and/or asthenia; or (viii) confusion and/or disorientation.
- Ketonuria shall mean a moderate or large urine nitroprusside reaction (color matches or exceeds 3+ or 40 mg/dL sample swatch for test strip).
- Ketonemia shall mean a capillary blood \beta-hydroxybutyrate concentration &gt;3.0 mM or a moderate or large plasma nitroprusside reaction (&gt;1.0 mM).
L3012: Overall, 19 suspected events were sent for adjudication (Table 214). There were few confirmed DKA events in the clinical program for bexagliflozin (two and three confirmed DKA events in bexagliflozin and placebo-exposed subjects, respectively). In trial C-476, there were more events of confirmed DKA in the placebo group as compared to the bexagliflozin group (bexagliflozin: one event (0.09%), placebo: three events (0.5%)). This imbalance became increasingly favorable to drug when events adjudicated as confirmed or probable DKA were pooled (bexagliflozin: one event (0.09%), placebo: five events (0.9%)). Only one event of confirmed DKA occurred in the remainder of the bexagliflozin program in Trial C-419 (bexagliflozin: one event (0.6%), placebo: zero events (0%).
L3013: Narratives for the two confirmed DKA events in the bexagliflozin group were reviewed. Subject 419-(b)(6) was a 37-year-old white male enrolled in C-419. The narrative reports that the subject presented to the hospital on Day 33 with epigastric pain, nausea, dehydration, and emesis following a binge drinking episode. The subject's severe anion gap metabolic acidosis was accompanied by high blood lactic acid levels, thought to be exacerbated by hypoperfusion and possible sepsis as well as concurrent metformin use. The discharge diagnosis was DKA/lactic acidosis secondary to alcohol abuse and metformin. Subject 476-(b)(6) was a 40-year-old white female enrolled in C-476. On Day 39, the subject presented to the hospital with diffuse abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting and diarrhea, and was hospitalized. The subject was rehydrated with intravenous fluid plus bicarbonate.
L3014: As discussed in Section 17.4, transient decreases in mean serum bicarbonate occurred in the placebo-controlled pool starting at Week 2 and recovering by Week 18, with a maximum mean decrease of -1.4 mEq/L in the bexagliflozin group compared to -0.5 mEq/L in the placebo group at Week 6. Transient decreases in serum bicarbonate were also observed in C-476 and C-448 although to a lesser extent. In line with these results, there were also more subjects who experienced at least one level 1 (&lt;20 mEq/L), 2 (&lt;18 mEq/L), and 3 (&lt;15 mEq/L) low bicarbonate values in the bexagliflozin group of the placebo-controlled pool compared to the placebo group. As few events of DKA occurred in the clinical program, the meaningfulness of this laboratory data is unclear.
L3015: ***FDA Reviewer Comment:*** The DKA monitoring and assessment procedures appear adequate to have identified and consistently classified events. While the small number of DKA events in the clinical program limits interpretability, it is reassuring that an excess of DKA events was not observed with bexagliflozin exposure. As with other SGLT2 inhibitors, premarket programs are unlikely to adequately assess DKA risk, and class labeling appears warranted.

L3021: ## 17.3.7. Renal Events
L3022: AKI, secondary to volume depletion in the setting of SGLT2 inhibitor treatment, is currently described in the Warnings and Precautions section of the US prescribing information across the class. While postmarketing events of AKI have been observed for approved SGLT2 inhibitors, there is increasing evidence that SGLT2 inhibitor treatment may be renal protective in patients with chronic kidney disease, slowing the decline in eGFR and progression to end-stage renal disease, and reducing renal-related mortality, independent of its effects on glycemic control (Gilbert and Thorpe 2019; Menne et al. 2019; Sridhar et al. 2020). In this section, renal function laboratory data and renal events, including AKI, are reviewed.
L3023: ## Renal Function Tests
L3024: Initiation of SGLT2 inhibitor treatment causes modest increases in serum creatinine and decreases in eGFR, an effect that is also observed with bexagliflozin. Maximum changes in serum creatinine and eGFR generally occur within six to twelve weeks of starting therapy and then stabilize. In the placebo-controlled pool, enrolling subjects primarily with normal renal function, changes in serum creatinine and eGFR were generally similar between treatment groups (Figure 74). However, changes in renal function were variable depending on the subject population evaluated. As discussed in Section 7.7.2, in C-448 enrolling subjects with stage 3 CKD, serum creatinine increased 0.14 mg/dL (10.8%) and eGFR decreased -4.6 mL/min/1.73 m2 from baseline to Week 6 in the bexagliflozin group, as compared to an increase in serum creatinine of 0.01 mg/dL (0.7%) and a decrease in eGFR of -0.08 mL/min/1.73 m2.

L3039: ## Renal Events
L3040: AKI events, as identified by the AKI FMQ, that occurred in C-476 are shown in Table 216. Renal failure events were prespecified as AESIs in the protocol for this trial, although no special procedures were implemented to identify or appropriately classify or document these events. A higher incidence of AKI events was observed in the bexagliflozin group (2.2% of subjects) than the placebo group (1.6% of subjects). However, there was no imbalance in AKI events between groups when the analysis was limited to serious events, with 0.8% and 0.7% of subjects experiencing events in the bexagliflozin and placebo groups; respectively. Three subjects (0.26%) assigned to the bexagliflozin group and two subjects (0.35%) assigned to the placebo group stopped dosing as a result of an AKI event. A random selection of narratives from serious AKI events were reviewed. While some AKI events occurred in the setting of hypotension/volume depletion, alternative etiologies that could have contributed to or caused the events were also present.
L3041: No AKI events occurred in the bexagliflozin groups of the placebo-controlled pool or active-controlled trials. AKI events occurring in C-448 enrolling subjects with moderate renal impairment are reviewed in Section 7.7.2.
L3042: **FDA Reviewer Comment:** As discussed in the next section, SGLT2 inhibitor treatment, including treatment with bexagliflozin, is associated with volume depletion and hypotension, and current labeling for approved SGLT2 inhibitors describes the potential risk of AKI secondary to volume depletion as Warnings and Precautions. Similar labeling appears appropriate for bexagliflozin.

L3047: ## 17.3.8. Volume Depletion/Hypotension Events
L3048: SGLT2 inhibitors are associated with osmotic diuresis and thus volume depletion and hypotension events are of concern for this drug class. FMQs for “Volume Depletion,” “Hypotension,” “Dizziness,” and “Syncope” were utilized to characterize the impact of osmotic diuresis in subjects treated with bexagliflozin.
L3049: An imbalance unfavorable to drug in hypotension events was observed, with 48 (4.2%) and 15 (2.6%) subjects experiencing a hypotension event in the bexagliflozin and placebo groups of C-476, respectively. All events were nonserious, with one event in a bexagliflozin-treated subject leading to treatment discontinuation. While events of dizziness may be nonspecific to volume depletion events, an excess of these events in the bexagliflozin group was also observed (7.3% versus 5.1% of subjects in the bexagliflozin and placebo groups having an event, respectively). Twelve (1.1%) and four subjects (0.7%) experienced at least one volume depletion event in the bexagliflozin and placebo groups, respectively. All events identified were events of dehydration. One dehydration event in the bexagliflozin group led to treatment discontinuation. There were more serious dehydration events in the placebo group as compared to the bexagliflozin group. AKI is a potentially serious consequence of volume depletion. Three of the 12 subjects who experienced dehydration in the bexagliflozin group had six events of AKI, of which two were SAEs. No events of AKI were observed in the four subjects who experienced dehydration in the placebo group. See Section 17.3.7 for additional discussion regarding AKI events. There were more subjects who experienced a syncope event in the placebo group than the bexagliflozin group. Events related to volume depletion events were limited in other trials, limiting interpretability. Overall, labeling similar to other members of the drug class appears appropriate.

L3055: ## 17.3.9. UTI Including Pyelonephritis and Urosepsis
L3056: Treatment with SGLT2 inhibitors increases the risk for UTIs due to increased glucosuria. Serious UTIs including pyelonephritis and urosepsis requiring hospitalization have been reported in subjects receiving SGLT2 inhibitors, and the risk of pyelonephritis and urosepsis is currently included as a Warnings and Precautions statement in the US prescribing information for approved products. These events were considered AESIs in the bexagliflozin clinical program.
L3057: UTI events occurring in the placebo-controlled pool are discussed in Section 7.6.1.3. The FMQ for “Renal and Urinary Tract Infection” was utilized to query for UTI events in C-476. In accordance with data from the placebo-controlled pool, there were more events of UTI in the bexagliflozin group (148 [13.1%] subjects with at least one event) as compared to the placebo group (68 [12.0%]). There was a minor imbalance that was unfavorable to bexagliflozin for UTI-related AEs leading to treatment discontinuation with bexagliflozin (0.8%) as compared to placebo (0.5%). There was no meaningful imbalance in events of pyelonephritis or urosepsis in the bexagliflozin group (11 [1.0%] subjects with at least one event) as compared to the placebo group (6 [1.1%]) as determined by a grouped query of the following PTs: pyelonephritis, pyelonephritis acute, urosepsis, kidney infection. As described in Section 7.6.1.3, upon review of SAE narratives for sepsis events, four events of sepsis in the bexagliflozin group and one event of sepsis in the placebo group appeared secondary to UTI. Addition of sepsis events to the analysis for pyelonephritis and urosepsis did not significantly change the interpretation of results. Regarding the remainder of the phase 3 program, only one other event of pyelonephritis occurred in a bexagliflozin treated subject in C-480.
L3058: ***FDA Reviewer Comment:*** *Overall, the small number of events of pyelonephritis and urosepsis limit interpretability of the data, although it is reassuring that no meaningful imbalances were observed in the available data. As increased risk of pyelonephritis and urosepsis is considered a class effect, labeling similar to other approved products appears appropriate.*

L3063: ## 17.3.10. GMI
L3064: Treatment with SGLT2 inhibitors, including bexagliflozin, increases the risk for GMI. GMI is proposed for inclusion in the labeling by the Applicant, both as a commonly occurring adverse reaction and as a Warnings and Precautions. GMI in the placebo-controlled pool is discussed in Section 7.6.1.3. The following section focus on clinically meaningful events of GMI in phase 3 trials not included in the placebo-controlled pool.
L3065: All phase 3 trials demonstrated a higher incidence of GMI in the bexagliflozin group as compared to comparator groups. In C-476, 9.0% and 2.8% of subjects had at least one event of GMI in the bexagliflozin and placebo groups, respectively, as identified by a customized Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities query (CMQ) developed by the Applicant (Table 219). GMIs occurred throughout the study with an onset from 3 to 1129 days after randomization (Applicant's analysis). One subject (476-(b)(6)) in the bexagliflozin group experienced an episode of severe vulvovaginal candidiasis that was not considered an SAE by the investigator. No SAEs of GMI were reported, although 14 subjects (1.2%), all in the bexagliflozin group, ceased dosing due to GMI (Applicant's analysis). The Applicant reports that five male subjects developed phimosis in C-476, four (0.4%) in the bexagliflozin group and one (0.2%) in the placebo group, and surgery/circumcision was performed or planned for all subjects in the bexagliflozin group. Information describing phimosis potentially leading to circumcision should be included in the labeling.

L3070: ## 17.3.11. Hypoglycemia
L3071: Insulin and insulin secretagogues (e.g., sulfonylureas) are known to cause hypoglycemia. The risk of hypoglycemia may be increased when an SGLT2 inhibitor is used in combination with insulin or insulin secretagogues, and this risk is currently labeled as a Warning and Precaution in approved SGLT2 inhibitor drugs and will be similarly included in the bexagliflozin labeling. In all clinical trials, subjects were provided with a glucometer and diary for recording blood glucose measurements and signs and symptoms that may be related to hypoglycemia. Subjects were also advised to perform daily fasting blood glucose measurements and record results. Hypoglycemia was defined in the clinical program into the following five categories: severe hypoglycemia, documented symptomatic hypoglycemia, asymptomatic hypoglycemia, probable symptomatic hypoglycemia, and relative hypoglycemia. Severe hypoglycemia was defined as an event requiring third party assistance for recovery. All other hypoglycemia categories relied on blood glucose cutoff of 70 mg/dL (level 1 hypoglycemia). As 70 mg/dL is generally considered an alert value where action should be taken to prevent further reductions in blood glucose, a re-analysis of the trial data was requested to assess level 2 hypoglycemia using the cutoff of &lt;54 mg/dL (American Diabetes Association Professional Practice et al. 2022a).
L3072: Severe hypoglycemia and level 2 hypoglycemia in placebo-controlled studies is presented in **Table 220**. Events rates for severe hypoglycemia and level 2 hypoglycemia were low in all placebo-controlled trials, generally occurring in trials where background insulin or sulfonylurea use was allowed. While it is reassuring that excess hypoglycemia was not observed with bexagliflozin, limited data impedes meaningful interpretation.

L3080: ## 17.3.12. Fournier's Gangrene
L3081: Based on postmarketing reports of cases of necrotizing fasciitis of the perineum (Fournier's gangrene) associated with use of SGLT2 inhibitors, a potential safety signal for this adverse event was identified by the Division of Pharmacovigilance-I (DPV-1) and a Tracked Safety Issue was opened (TSI #1844) in 2018. The DPV-I review identified 12 cases of Fournier's gangrene associated with SGLT2 inhibitor use in the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System database and medical literature, prompting a Drug Safety Communication on August 28, 2018 and concurrent Safety Labeling Change that added Fournier's gangrene to the Warnings and Precautions section of the US prescribing information and patient Medication Guide for all products in the SGLT2 inhibitor class.
L3082: One case of Fournier's gangrene was reported by the Applicant in a nondiabetic subject in the randomized withdrawal essential hypertension Trial C-603B. Subject 603-(b)(6) was a 63-year-old, white, non-Hispanic male who developed Fournier's gangrene while randomized to bexagliflozin in the run-in period of C-603B. An abdominal/pelvic CT scan showed scrotal wall thickening, subcutaneous emphysema, as well as enlarged retroperitoneal and pelvic sidewall lymph nodes. He was treated with operative scrotal exploration and IV antibiotics. Notably, medical history included HIV infection and prior surgery and prosthesis involving the scrotum. The event was assessed as not likely related to the investigational product by the investigator. Given the noted risk factors and potential alternative etiology, drug causality of the event cannot be determined. Nonetheless, given that Fournier's gangrene cannot be adequately assessed in the premarket program conducted and given that it is considered a class effect, a Warnings and Precautions statement will be included in the labeling.
L3083: ## 17.3.13. Revascularization Procedures
L3084: As described in Section 7.7.1, the Applicant used a dedicated CRF to capture information on amputation and revascularization procedures. See Section 7.7.1 for a detailed review of amputation events. With regards to revascularization procedures, the CRF prompted the investigator to select one of the following procedure types: cardiac catheterization, percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), coronary artery bypass graft (CABG), revascularization for peripheral artery disease (PAD), carotid artery stenosis with revascularization, cardiac transplant, or other (if other was selected, investigators were asked to specify additional information). The revascularization procedures that occurred in C-476 are shown in Table 221. An imbalance was observed for the number of CABG procedures that occurred in C-476 (2.5% versus 0.7% in the bexagliflozin and placebo groups, respectively). The Applicant posits that this imbalance may represent a favorable drug effect, as patients chosen for CABG must be healthy enough to withstand major surgery and a selection bias in which candidates from the active arm were judged to be more fit for surgery may have been present. This seems an unlikely explanation given what is known about bexagliflozin's beneficial effects over the course of the trial. Overall, the meaningfulness of the imbalance in CABG procedures is unclear, but the results from the MACE meta-analysis provide reassurance that bexagliflozin does not increase the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events.

L3089: ## 17.3.14. Cardiovascular Safety
L3090: To show that bexagliflozin was not associated with an excess CV risk, a MACE meta-analysis was performed according to the recommendations in the FDA Guidance titled *Evaluating Cardiovascular Risk in New Antidiabetic Therapies to Treat Type 2 Diabetes* (December 2008). This Guidance document represented the agency's current thinking while the bexagliflozin clinical program was being completed. While this Guidance has since been withdrawn and replaced with the Guidance document titled *Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: Evaluating the Safety of New Drugs for Improving Glycemic Control* (March 2020), the evaluation of cardiovascular safety performed by the Applicant is adequate to evaluate the impact of bexagliflozin on cardiovascular safety.
L3091: A detailed review of the MACE meta-analysis is presented in Section 17.1. In short, the upper bound of the 95% confidence interval for the HR for major adverse cardiovascular events defined by a four-point composite endpoint (cardiovascular death, stroke, myocardial infarction, or hospitalization for unstable angina) was less than 1.8 (HR: 0.80 [0.58, 1.09]) and the upper bound of the 95% confidence interval for the hazard ratio defined by a three point composite endpoint (cardiovascular death, stroke, or myocardial infarction) was less than 1.3 (HR: 0.82
L3092: [0.59, 1.13]). The upper bound in the latter case was greater than unity and hence superiority to comparator for reduction of risk was not established. The conclusions were corroborated by several sensitivity analyses. HRs favorable to bexagliflozin were observed for all subcomponents with the exception of the risk of nonfatal stroke (HR: 1.2 [0.59, 2.46]), which may be due to few events observed in this category. Subgroup analyses did not identify any meaningful differences in HR by age, sex, race, geographical region, body mass index, disease duration, disease severity, renal function, or systolic blood pressure. Overall, exposure to bexagliflozin is not expected to unacceptably increase the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events in diabetic patients.
L3093: ## 17.4. Laboratory Findings
L3094: Blood samples for the evaluation of hematology, chemistry, and lipid parameters were collected and assessed in all trials. Sampling timepoints varied by trial, but generally occurred at screening, at the end of treatment (typically Week 24), and at the follow-up safety visit (typically Week 26), as well as at prespecified intervals during each trial, e.g., every 6 to 12 weeks. Urinalysis was also routinely performed, although results of urine glucose in urinalysis reports were suppressed as not to unblind treatment assignment. The placebo-controlled pool was deemed appropriate to characterize changes in laboratory parameters following bexagliflozin exposure. In the analyses utilizing the placebo-controlled pool representing change in laboratory parameters over time, data from the Week 14 follow-up visit from C-449 is excluded, and only Trials C-419 and C-450 contribute to the Week 18, 24, and 26 timepoints. Data from other trials (e.g., C-448 and C-476) are also presented where appropriate.
L3095: ## Hematology
L3096: The SGLT2 inhibitor pharmacologic class is associated with small increases in hemoglobin and hematocrit, which may be attributable to osmotic diuresis and hemoconcentration. In the placebo-controlled pool, a mean increase of 0.4 g/dL (2.7%) hemoglobin and 1.3% hematocrit was observed from baseline to Week 24 in the bexagliflozin group, which remained slightly elevated at the Week 26 follow-up visit, as opposed to a slight mean decrease in each parameter in the placebo group (Figure 76). Increases in these parameters were slightly more pronounced in C-476 and C-448 (data not shown). As shown in Table 222, a higher proportion of subjects had hemoglobin increases &gt;2 g/dL and &gt;3 g/dL from baseline in the bexagliflozin group compared to the placebo group in all trials.
L3097: It is clinically plausible that increases in hemoglobin and hematocrit could lead to an increased likelihood of experiencing a thromboembolic event. As discussed in Section 17.1, the results from the MACE+ meta-analysis were overall favorable to bexagliflozin. The nonfatal stroke component of the MACE+ meta-analysis demonstrated a point estimate that was unfavorable to bexagliflozin (HR: 1.2; 95% CI: 0.6, 2.5); however, limited events produced wide confidence intervals that limit the interpretability of this data. Several additional analyses were completed to address this concern utilizing data from C-476, which enrolled a subject population that may be more likely to experience a thromboembolic event as compared to other trials in the clinical program. In addition, approximately 21% of subjects in C-476 had at least one hemoglobin result &gt;2 g/dL above their baseline value (Table 222). As shown in Table 222, there were proportionally fewer thromboembolic events in the bexagliflozin group compared to the placebo
L3098: group as assessed by FMQs for “Thrombosis,” “Thrombosis (Arterial),” and “Thrombosis (Venous),” as well as a CMQ that has been previously developed and utilized to assess potentially meaningful thromboembolic events associated with SGLT2 inhibitor treatment. Overall, thromboembolic events do not appear to be a safety issue for bexagliflozin based on the results in this clinical program, but a meta-analysis of events across the class might better inform this potential safety signal, which has a mechanistically plausible basis.
L3099: There were no meaningful differences in central tendencies between the bexagliflozin group and the placebo group in the placebo-controlled pool for other hematology parameters, i.e., leukocytes, platelets, eosinophils, lymphocytes, and neutrophils (Figure 76). Regarding the proportion of subjects with one or more values exceeding specified levels for hematology parameters (Table 222), a difference was observed in subjects who experienced one or more level 1 (&lt;1000 cells/uL) decreases in lymphocyte values between the bexagliflozin group (5.6%) and the placebo group (1.7%) in the placebo-controlled pool, which was not observed in other trials. The clinical significance of this finding is unclear, although it is notable that an increased incidence in the system organ class of “Infections and Infestations” was not observed in the placebo-controlled pool (16.1% versus 17.7% in the bexagliflozin and placebo groups, respectively).

L3140: ## Lipids
L3141: Fasting lipid measurements were completed in all trials, and subjects were queried to assess compliance with an approximately 10 hours fast prior to blood draw to ensure lipid parameters could be accurately assessed. Small increases in low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) have been associated with the SGLT2 inhibitor pharmacologic class, and changes in LDL-C are currently described in the labeling for approved products. In the placebo-controlled pool, mean changes in LDL-C of 1.5 mg/dL (1.4%) and -3.3 mg/dL (-3.1%) were observed from baseline to Week 24 in the bexagliflozin and placebo groups, respectively (Figure 77). LDL-C was also slightly elevated within the first 24 weeks of treatment of Trial C-476, with mean changes from baseline to Week 24 of 3.1 mg/dL (4.1%) and 2.5 (3.2%) mg/dL in the bexagliflozin and placebo groups, respectively, although these elevations decreased over time with mean changes returning to baseline in both groups by Week 72 (data not shown). No consistent trends were observed in C-476 regarding the proportion of subjects with at least one value exceeding certain LDL-C thresholds; however, there was a greater proportion of subjects who had at least one value that exceeded level 1 (&gt;130 mg/dL) and level 2 (&gt;160 mg/dL) in the bexagliflozin group as compared to the placebo group in the placebo-controlled pool and C-448 (Table 224). Regarding other lipid parameters, small increases in high-density lipoprotein cholesterol were observed, with mean changes from baseline to Week 24 of 2.2 (4.3%) mg/dL and -0.2 (-0.4%) mg/dL in the bexagliflozin and placebo groups, respectively, of the placebo-controlled pool. There was also a decrease in triglycerides, with mean changes from baseline at Week 24 of -16 mg/dL (-9.3%) and -6.9 (-3.4%) mg/dL in the bexagliflozin and placebo groups, respectively.
L3142: ***FDA Reviewer Comment:*** As presented in Section 17.1, the MACE+ meta-analysis supports that bexagliflozin is not associated with increased risk for MACE, providing reassuring evidence that the small changes in lipid parameters described herein do not adversely impact cardiac safety.

L3154: ## Liver Chemistry
L3155: ALT, AST, and total and direct bilirubin were measured in all trials. Alkaline phosphatase was also measured in all trials with the exception of C-448 and in C-450. In the placebo-controlled pool, there were no meaningful changes in central tendencies in liver chemistry parameters, with minor decreases in ALT, AST, and alkaline phosphatase between baseline and Week 24 (Figure 78). Results were comparable in Trials C-476 and C-448 (data not shown). Outlier enzyme elevations were generally balanced between treatment groups. See Section 17.3.5 Hepatic Injury for additional analysis of potential DILI events.

L3175: ## Chemistry
L3176: In the placebo-controlled pool, no meaningful changes were observed from baseline to Week 24 in mean sodium, potassium, chloride, calcium, protein, and albumin (Figure 79).
L3177: Magnesium is regulated by the urinary system and hypermagnesemia is most often associated with renal impairment in the absence of overdose scenarios, making this laboratory marker relevant in assessing the impact of bexagliflozin on renal function. Clinical symptoms such as nausea, lethargy, and headache may be seen when plasma levels exceed 4.8 mg/dL, while concentrations higher than 7.2 mg/dL are associated with hypocalcemia, hypotension, bradycardia, and EKG changes. There was an increase of 0.13 mg/dL (6.8%) in magnesium levels in the bexagliflozin group compared to a -0.01 mg/dL (0.5%) decrease in the placebo group in the placebo-controlled pool at week 24, which returned approximately to baseline levels after drug withdrawal at the follow-up visit. Increases of approximately 0.32 mg/dL (18%) and 0.21 mg/dL (10%) from baseline to Week 24 were also observed in the bexagliflozin groups of C-476 and C-448, respectively, as compared to an increase of 0.1 mg/dL (5%) and a decrease of -0.02 mg/dL (1%) in the respective placebo groups. In line with these results, the placebo-controlled pool, C-476, and C-448 had a higher proportion of subjects with level 1 (&gt;2.3 mg/dL) increases in magnesium in the bexagliflozin group compared to the placebo group in each trial, although it is reassuring that no subjects had magnesium values meeting the criteria for level 2 (&gt;4 mg/dL) or Level 3 (&gt;7 mg/dL) (Table 226). In addition, a search for AEs indicative of elevated magnesium levels (i.e., PTs of “hypermagnesemia” or “blood magnesium increased”) in bexagliflozin-exposed subjects did not reveal any events in any trial. While not currently described in the labeling for approved SGLT2 inhibitors, increases in serum magnesium associated with SGLT2 inhibitor treatment have been noted in prior clinical reviews (see Dr. Hyon’s review for canagliflozin in DARRTS dated August 10, 2012) and reported in the literature (Tang et al. 2016; Sasaki et al. 2017; Ray et al. 2020). The magnitude of serum magnesium elevations observed in the clinical program do not appear clinically concerning.
L3178: Transient decreases in mean serum bicarbonate occurred in the placebo-controlled pool, with a maximum mean decrease of -1.4 mEq/L in the bexagliflozin group compared to -0.5 mEq/L in the placebo group at Week 6. Transient decreases were also observed in C-476 and C-448 although to a lesser extent (data not shown). In line with these results, there were also more subjects who experienced at least one level 1 (&lt;20 mEq/L), 2 (&lt;18 mEq/L), and 3 (&lt;15 mEq/L) low bicarbonate values in the bexagliflozin groups of the placebo-controlled pool and C-476 compared to the placebo groups (Table 226). Similar trends were also observed for the proportion of subjects with values exceeding level 1 and 2 low bicarbonate values for C-448. The clinical meaningfulness of these findings is unclear. As discussed in Section 17.3.6, there was no signal for DKA observed in the bexagliflozin clinical program; however, the event rate of DKA may be too low to adequately assess in a premarket setting.
L3179: Serum phosphate increased 0.23 mg/dL (6.6%) in the bexagliflozin group as compared to 0.02 mg/dL (0.6%) in the placebo group from baseline to Week 24 in the placebo-controlled pool. Similar trends were observed in C-476 and C-448 (data not shown). Minor increases in serum phosphate levels have been previously characterized (e.g., see US prescribing information for ertugliflozin).

L3232: ## 17.5. Vital Signs
L3233: The Applicant assessed changes in blood pressure and heart rate in the clinical program. In the placebo-controlled pool, a small mean reduction in SBP from baseline to Week 24 occurred in the bexagliflozin group as opposed to a small mean increase in the placebo group (Figure 80). Blood pressure changes were evaluated as secondary efficacy endpoints in the clinical program and additional information characterizing the drug effect on blood pressure can be found in Section 6.2.3.3. In addition, refer to Section 17.3.8 for additional information regarding an assessment of hypotension in the clinical program. There were no noteworthy changes in heart rate between treatment groups (data not shown).

L3237: ## 17.6. QT
L3238: The Applicant conducted a thorough QT (TQT) study (C-428) to assess the proarrhythmic potential of bexagliflozin. The protocol for this study was reviewed by the Agency prior to its initiation under IND 103822. In this randomized, partially-blinded, three-period crossover study, 37 healthy subjects received bexagliflozin 100 mg (capsule formulation), placebo, and a single oral dose of moxifloxacin 400 mg. The Applicant's TQT study results were reviewed by the Interdisciplinary Review Team for Cardiac Safety Studies (IRT-CS), and their independent analysis yielded similar results to those reported by the Applicant. The IRT-CS states that the studied dose of 100 mg meets the recommendation for exposure coverage in a TQT study. The IRT-CS confirmed that C-428, conducted using the capsule formulation of bexagliflozin, is adequate to support the QT assessment for the to-be-marketed tablet formulation. The largest upper bound of the 2-sided 90% CI for the mean difference between bexagliflozin and placebo was below 10 ms, which is the threshold for regulatory concern as described in ICH E14 guidelines (Table 227). The IRT-CS concluded that a single dose of 100 mg bexagliflozin does not cause drug-related QT prolongation (DARRTS review under NDA 214373 dated December 6, 2021 and under IND 103822 dated November 4, 2013). These findings are in accordance with nonclinical studies, which indicated a low potential for QT prolongation.
L3239: **Table 227. The Point Estimates and the 90% CIs Corresponding to the Largest Upper Bounds for Bexagliflozin and the Largest Lower Bound for Moxifloxacin, Trial C-428**
L3240: Treatment	Time (hour)	\Delta\Delta\text{QTcF} (ms)	90% CI (ms)
Bexagliflozin 100 mg	10	2.4	(0.6, 4.2)

L3241: Source: IRT-CS Review under IND 103822 dated November 4, 2013 in DARRTS
L3242: *Bonferroni adjustment of 3 time points was applied
L3243: Regarding other safety findings from C-428, there were no deaths, SAEs, or AEs of clinical importance per ICH E14 guidelines (e.g., syncope, seizures, significant ventricular arrhythmias, sudden cardiac death) that occurred in this study. Subjects who experienced a PR interval &gt;200 ms or a QRS interval &gt;100 ms were generally balanced between bexagliflozin and placebo treatment periods (data not shown).
L3244: ## 17.7. Safety Analyses by Demographic Subgroups
L3245: Safety analyses by demographic subgroup utilizing the placebo-controlled pool and C-476 were performed to evaluate whether commonly occurring events and AESIs differed importantly between subgroups (Table 228 and Table 229). For the placebo-controlled pool, grouped queries (GQs) were utilized to align with analyses of this data pool presented in Section 6 and in the labeling, and commonly occurring AEs (i.e., &gt;2% and greater in the bexagliflozin group than the placebo group) are presented. For C-476, CMQs derived by the Applicant were utilized to examine AESIs by subgroup, and selected AESIs are presented. A trend between increased BMI quartile and female GMI events in subjects treated with bexagliflozin was observed in both the placebo-controlled pool and C-476. There were no concerning trends regarding age &gt;65 years and increased incidence of adverse reactions in either analysis. More females had UTI events in both bexagliflozin and placebo groups.

L3351: Diagram illustrating the mechanism of action of Bexagliflozin. Glucose enters the proximal tubule. In the S1 segment (~90% reabsorption), glucose is reabsorbed via SGLT2. In the S2/S3 segment (~10% reabsorption), glucose is reabsorbed via SGLT1. SGLT2 inhibitors block the SGLT2 transporter in the S1 segment, preventing glucose reabsorption and leading to glucosuria.

L3353: Figure 3 displays two bar charts illustrating the reduction of HbA1c in diabetic mice and rats treated with bexagliflozin.
The left chart, titled "db/db mouse," shows HbA1c (%) versus Pre-dose and 28d Post-dose. The Y-axis ranges from 4 to 10. The legend indicates five groups: Control, 0.1 mg/kg, 0.3 mg/kg, 1 mg/kg, and 3 mg/kg. At Pre-dose, all groups show similar HbA1c levels (around 7.5-8%). At 28d Post-dose, the Control group shows a significant increase (around 8.5%). The legend indicates five groups: 10% PEG400, 0.1 EGT1474, 0.3 EGT1474, 1.0 EGT1474, and 3.0 EGT1474. At Day 0, all groups show similar HbA1c levels (around 9.5-10%). At Day 29, the treated groups (0.1, 0.3, 1.0, and 3.0 EGT1474) show a dose-dependent reduction in HbA1c compared to the 10% PEG400 group. The 3.0 EGT1474 group shows the lowest HbA1c (around 7.5%). The DELTA column shows the percentage change from Day 0 to Day 29. The 3.0 EGT1474 group shows a significant reduction (around -2.5%), while the 10% PEG400 group shows a slight increase (around 0.5%). Asterisks (**) indicate statistical significance for the DELTA change compared to the 10% PEG400 group.
L3354: Figure 4 is a line graph titled "Model Predicted Dose-Response Relationship in THR-1442-C-449". The X-axis represents the Bexagliflozin Dose in mg (0, 5, 10, 15, 20). The Y-axis represents the HbA1c Change from Baseline in % (ranging from -0.6 to 0.4). The graph shows a dose-response relationship where HbA1c change decreases (becomes more negative) as the dose increases. Observed mean changes from baseline are marked by black dots at doses 0 mg, 5 mg, 10 mg, and 20 mg. The model predictions, based on parameter estimates, are shown by a middle black line, with upper and lower bounds of the 95% confidence interval represented by the top and bottom black lines, respectively. The model predicts that the HbA1c change decreases from approximately 0.2% at 0 mg to approximately -0.4% at 20 mg.

L3394: Diagram showing the 1st order absorption (Ka) + lag-time model. The model consists of three compartments: Absorption Compartment, Central Compartment, and Peripheral Compartment. Dose enters the Absorption Compartment. The Absorption Compartment transfers to the Central Compartment via Ka (ALAG). The Central Compartment transfers to the Peripheral Compartment via Q/Vc and back to the Central Compartment via Q/Vp. Elimination occurs from the Central Compartment via CL/Vc.
L3395: Figure 39 displays the Goodness-of-Fit (GOF) plots for the Final PopPK Model, organized into three rows of plots, each corresponding to a different dependent variable (DV): DV (Observed), IPRED (Individual Predicted), and CWRES (Conditional Weighted Residuals). The plots are arranged by dose (mg) in columns: 3 mg, 5 mg, 10 mg, 15 mg, 20 mg, 30 mg, and 90 mg.
The DV plots show observed data (black open circles) against predicted values (PRED or IPRED). The black dashed line represents the line of unity or identity, and the blue line represents a fitted linear or loess smooth line. The DV plots generally show a strong correlation between observed and predicted values across all doses.
The CWRES plots show the conditional weighted residuals (CWRES) against time after dose (TAD). The residuals are centered around zero, indicating a good fit of the model to the data.
